jobs.details_text:
Editorial Assistant 
Department: Research and Higher Education (RHED)
Responsible to: Managing Editor
Location: South Kensington, London SW7. Option to work from home one or two days a week, dependent on the event schedule
Hours: Full Time. 35-hour working week
Contract: Permanent. Subject to successful completion of a probationary period of three months.
Salary: £31,200- £32,930 per annum, depending on experience and qualifications
About Us: 
The Royal Geographical Society (with the Institute of British Geographers) is the learned society and professional body for geography and geographers. It is also a charity and a membership organisation. The Society was founded in 1830 and has been one of the most active of the learned societies ever since. It was pivotal in establishing geography as a teaching and research discipline in British universities and continues to play a key role in geographical and environmental education.
About You and the Role 
The RGS-IBG publish five peer-reviewed geography journals, four of which are managed by the RGS-IBG Managing Editor: Transactions of the Institute of British Geographers (TIBG) , The Geographical Journal , Area , and Geo: Geography and Environment . The Society also publishes an open-access Book Series with LSE Press, the blog Geography Directions and a series of guides and advice on publishing.
The editorial assistant will report to the Managing Editor of Academic Publications, providing support for this suite of publications.
This is an exciting opportunity to develop a greater understanding of the academic peer review and publishing process and provides an excellent opportunity to work with the academic community.
The role is ideally suited to someone with very strong organisational and communication skills and an understanding and interest in contemporary academic geography.
Duties and responsibilities 
Administrative tasks:
Lead on screening for all journal submissions – conducting initial checks for anonymity,word length, formatting, (mis)use of AI, publishing integrity issues.
Maintain a record of all submitted papers.
Lead on checking files of accepted papers for production.
Assist authors with generating alt text for images and figures.
Support Managing Editor with day-to-day author and peer reviewer communication and inbox management.
Assist Managing Editor with proofreading accepted papers.
Support Managing Editor with finding potential peer reviewers for submitted papers.
Oversee Special Section administration and regularly liaise with Special Section organisers.
Upload blog posts to the Geography Directions WordPress website.
Responsibility for registering DOI numbers for blog posts and online resources.
Design and format guides and resources for the RGS website.
Support with social media strategy for the journals and the Book Series.
Schedule editorial board meetings and take minutes.
Assist with annual journal prize administration.
Organise book launch events for Book Series authors.
Support the journals’ and Book Series’ events at the RGS Annual Conference.
Support Managing Editor to run workshops for postgraduate students and early-career researchers.
Writing and editing tasks:
Work with selected authors to write monthly research spotlights on journal articles for the
RGS website.
Assess and edit blog submissions to Geography Directions blog from academic authors.
Selection Criteria 
Essential
An undergraduate degree or equivalent in Geography
Demonstrable knowledge of contemporary academic geography
An interest in scholarly publishing
Excellent attention to detail
Systematic approach to tasks
Strong written language skills
Strong organisational skills
Ability to prioritise and balance multiple everyday tasks at once
Ability to work independently and as part of a team
Basic familiarity with Excel
Capability of working across multiple online platforms
Desirable
Experience of writing for public audiences
Proofreading experience
Administrative experience
Proven record of working effectively to deadlines
Ability to take initiative
Awareness of the (mis)use of AI in scholarly publishing
Salary and Benefits: 
This is a permanent, full-time post subject to successful completion of a probationary period of three months. The salary range for this post is £31,200- £32,930 per annum depending on experience and qualifications. The post is based in Kensington, London.
There are a range of benefits at the Society which include the following:
35-hour working week with Flexi time, dependent on the business needs.
Option to work from home one or two days a week, dependent on the event schedule. 
25 days annual leave per annum plus public bank holidays.
Society closure between Christmas and New Year, in addition to the basic annual leave allowance.
Pension scheme - 3% employee, 7.5% employer.
Group Life Assurance at four-times basic annual salary.
Corporate eye care vouchers.
Cycle to work scheme.
Free 24-hour Employee Assistance helpline with available counselling support.
Closing date: 12 noon on 23 November. 
Interviews are planned to take place on 2 or 3 December 2026. The interviews will also include a task.
Interested? 
If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. 
The Society aims to be an equal opportunities employer.
Applicants must have the right to work in the UK. The Society is unable to offer work visa sponsorships. We are committed to building an inclusive team and strongly encourage applications from those people who are traditionally underrepresented in the geographical discipline.
No agencies please.

jobs.details_text:
Our client is a large local government organisation and looking for an experienced Housing / Homelessness Coordinator to join their team. This is initially a 6 month contract which may be extended for the right applicant.
You will
To liaise with commissioned accommodation providers to share client information and determine suitability of placement in relation to placement size, risk management, statutory duty. 
Monitor and reduce the use of B&B especially for families and under 18s to ensure that Government targets are met. 
To record all placements on the accommodation management system and homelessness database. 
To continually review and manage 300+ placements across the range of accommodation settings (B&B, temporary accommodation, supported accommodation and off the streets accommodation and resettlement properties purchased through LAHF) in response to changing needs and circumstances of clients and households and to orchestrate a chain of internal moves to directly benefit customers. 
To provide a daily/ weekly report of activities including daily and pending placements, vacancies, voids and planned moves providing overall system understanding to providers and management ensuring individuals are best placed according to need. 
To produce a monthly accommodation summary evidencing total number of clients accommodated across the whole system including all council owned and commissioned stock including sport purchase, length of stay, status of homelessness applications, move-on options.
Through the approved management governance route, to spot purchase of bed and breakfast accommodation plus costs for internal moves to a maximum value of £25,000 pcm. 
Deal with all payment applications for host and other temporary accommodation arrangements including purchase orders and invoicing. 20. Processing all payments to refugees, hosts and landlords 
Maintain accurate records of payments made and reconciliation to floats and budget
Resolve all payment queries and problems 
Deal with changes reported and updating the Council Tax team of move-ins and move-outs
THIS ROLE IS INSIDE SCOPE OF IR35

Digital Communications Assistant 
Contract : Permanent
Grade/Salary : £27,024-£28,666 (pro rata)
Working hours: 7-10 hours per week
Work location : North Devon Outreach Centre/Exeter/Hybrid
Benefits: 25 days annual leave a year (pro rata), rising by 1 day a year until 5 years’ service – maximum 30 days (pro rata) plus bank holidays. 
North Devon Against Domestic Abuse is committed to equity and diversity and strongly encourages applicants with a disability, from ethnically diverse backgrounds and the LGBT community, as these groups are currently under-represented in our organisation. 
Job Summary
The Digital Communications Assistant will help NDADA and the Devon Domestic Abuse Alliance raise awareness of domestic abuse and the support available across Devon. They will create and schedule social media content, update websites, produce newsletters, manage mailing lists, design digital and printed resources, and support awareness campaigns and community engagement activities.
The postholder will work with NDADA teams and Alliance partners to gather information, turn it into clear and accessible communications, and promote services including Gateway, IDVA, DASW, counselling, courses, volunteering, partner services and fundraising. The role will support both external communications with the public, partners and stakeholders, and internal communications that keep staff, volunteers and partners informed and connected
The role will also support website improvements, digital projects and the introduction of new tools and technologies that improve communication, service delivery and organisational efficiency. Working alongside the Central Access and Business Development Manager, the postholder will help turn ideas into practical resources, systems and projects that benefit staff, partners and the people who use our services
Main Responsibilities 
Communications, Marketing and Engagement 
• Create, schedule and maintain content for social media, websites, newsletters, campaigns, case studies, printed materials and other communications, ensuring information is clear, accurate, accessible and engaging.
• Support awareness campaigns, fundraising activities, events and community engagement initiatives by preparing communications, resources and promotional materials. 
• Promote NDADA and DDAA services through accessible, trauma-informed and consistent communications, supporting the development of brand identity, marketing materials and communication resources
Digital Platforms and Content Development 
• Maintain and update website content, ensuring information is accurate, accessible and up to date. 
• Create and update digital resources for staff, partners and service users using approved platforms and software. 
• Use digital tools, including Microsoft 365, Canva, SharePoint, Teams and approved AI tools, to support communication, engagement and day-to-day administration. 
• Monitor online content and communications channels through analytics tools, making routine updates and highlighting issues or improvements where appropriate. 
• Support the identification, testing and implementation of approved digital tools and emerging technologies that improve communication, engagement, efficiency and service delivery. 
• Ensure digital systems, records and information are managed in accordance with organisational policies, safeguarding requirements, confidentiality standards, information governance principles, UK GDPR and Data Protection legislation.
Partnership Working and Organisational Support 
• Work collaboratively with NDADA colleagues, DDAA partners, volunteers and stakeholders, supporting communication, information sharing and the effective delivery of services, projects and organisational activities
• Assist with fundraising, volunteering, events, service development and other organisational activities, including preparing resources, maintaining records and supporting engagement activities where required. 
• Attend meetings, training and events as required, taking notes and supporting follow-up actions where appropriate.
• Maintain confidentiality and work in accordance with safeguarding, data protection, equality and organisational policies and procedures. 
• Undertake other reasonable duties consistent with the purpose and level of the role
To Apply 
If you feel you are a suitable candidate and would like to work for North Devon Against Domestic Abuse, please do not hesitate to apply.

jobs.details_text:
This is an opportunity for a sustainability policy professional to lead on circular economy policy issues helping to shape both industry practice and public policy. The role combines policy development, member engagement, stakeholder management and external representation, working at the forefront of sustainability challenges affecting a major UK sector.
Client Details 
Our client is a highly influential UK membership organisation representing one of the country's largest economic sectors. Acting as the voice of its members with government, regulators and key stakeholders, the organisation plays a central role in shaping policy, supporting industry collaboration and driving progress on major sustainability challenges facing UK businesses.
Description 
Sustainability Policy Adviser
Responsibilities:
Lead the development of policy positions across circular economy and sustainability priorities, representing the industry with government, regulators and stakeholders across the UK.
Monitor, analyse and influence policy and regulatory developments to help create a favourable policy environment that supports circularity.
Support members in understanding and responding to current and emerging compliance requirements.
Deliver consultation responses, guidance, briefings and general member communications that translate complex policy into practical insight.
Industry and thought leadership: their circular economy agenda by identifying emerging trends and opportunities, shaping industry thinking and developing member-led positions on topics.
Stakeholder engagement and industry collaboration: Build and maintain strong and effective relationships with members, government, regulators, trade associations, NGOs, commercial partners and other stakeholders to influence both policy outcomes and industry collaboration that supports circular economy and broader sustainability priorities.
Convene retailers and wider stakeholders through working groups, events, partnerships and collaborative initiatives that advance circular economy ambitions, support compliance, knowledge sharing, industry leadership and action on shared circularity challenges.
Communications and External representation: Represent them to external audiences, industry forums and media in collaboration with internal communications and media colleagues.
Sustainability Community management: Support and develop their Sustainability Community, strengthening member engagement, learning and new member interest, with a focus on circular economy priorities. Project manage events, workshops, webinars, policy updates and collaborative activity; work with partners where appropriate.
Profile 
Sustainability Policy Adviser
Essential:
Strong experience in sustainability, environmental policy or public affairs.
Good understanding of circular economy policy, including packaging, waste and resource management.
Experience developing policy positions, guidance or stakeholder-led initiatives.
Excellent stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence government, industry and wider partners.
Strong project management capabilities, able to deliver multiple priorities simultaneously.
Confident communicator, with experience producing briefings, reports and presentations for senior audiences.
Job Offer

London, hybrid (flexible)
What's on offer:
Permanent position

Flexible London hybrid policy

jobs.details_text:
Creative and Communications Executive 
Are you passionate about creative communications and love seeing your work make an impact? Here's your chance to join HACT and use your skills to show the real difference housing makes to people’s lives.
This is a varied, hands-on role in a small marketing team. Creative design and communication is the main focus bringing our brand, messages and stories to life. Alongside this, you'll bring solid marketing and communications experience, rolling up your sleeves to support campaigns, content and channels day to day. You'll work with colleagues across HACT and our customers, turning research, data and big ideas into work that is clear, credible and engaging.
About HACT 
HACT is the innovation charity for the social housing sector. For more than 65 years, we've worked with housing associations and partners to create better outcomes for residents and communities. Our work in social value, community investment and collaboration helps organisations understand the communities they serve and the impact they have.
What you'll do 
Creative 
Creative design: Design high-quality, on-brand assets for print and digital across all channels, using AI where appropriate while keeping HACT’s work authentic.
Campaign creative: Develop creative concepts and visual identities for multi-channel campaigns, from brief to delivery.
Data and insight: Turn research, data and complex messages into clear reports, infographics and data visualisation.
Brand and templates: Own HACT’s brand guidelines, asset library, templates and approvals, so the brand is used consistently by colleagues, associates and partners.
Motion and video: Produce short-form video, animation and motion graphics.
Creative workflow and suppliers: Scope briefs with stakeholders, prioritise creative requests and deliver to deadline, briefing external suppliers where needed.
Communications 
Copywriting: Write and edit copy, including articles, ghostwritten pieces, case studies, social posts, email and web content.
Social media: Develop, schedule and publish content that grows engagement across our platforms.
Email: Build and send targeted email campaigns through HubSpot.
Website: Update web content and landing pages with SEO, AEO and user experience in mind.
Events: Design materials for HACT’s conferences, webinars and external events, and support delivery.
Agents programme: Help build, test and improve AI agents and the knowledge banks they draw on.
Reporting: Track the performance of creative and content, and recommend improvements.
Governance: Make sure creative and communications meet HACT’s brand standards and use AI responsibly.
What you'll bring 
Essential 
A strong portfolio showing design across print and digital
Advanced skills in Adobe Creative Suite (InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop) and Canva
Marketing and communications experience across social media, email, website and content
Confident copywriting skills and a sharp eye for detail
Knowledge of AI design tools and how to use them responsibly
The ability to turn complex information into clear, accessible content
Excellent organisation, juggling multiple briefs and changing priorities
Confidence working with people at all levels and acting on feedback
Desirable 
Video editing and motion graphics skills
Experience of HubSpot or other CRMs and website CMSs
Experience briefing printers, agencies or freelancers
Interest in the housing, charity or social impact sectors
If you don't meet every point but have the skills to do the job well, we'd still love to hear from you.
What we offer 
£36,000 salary and 4–5% contributory pension
Annual leave allowance
Flexible and remote working
Learning and development support
Work that supports residents and communities across the UK
Our culture 
We're a small team with a big purpose. Our values shape how we work: supportive, transparent, respectful, kind, honest and collaborative. We're committed to a safe, inclusive environment for colleagues, customers, partners and communities.

Volunteer Coordinator 
Location: North Devon Outreach Centre/Hybrid
Salary: £25,455-£28,666 (pro rata)
Vacancy Type : 12 months fixed term, 20 hours per week 
Benefits: 25 days annual leave a year (pro rata), rising by 1 day a year until 5 years’ service – maximum 30 days plus bank holidays.
North Devon Against Domestic Abuse is committed to equity and diversity and strongly encourages applicants with a disability, from ethnically diverse backgrounds and the LGBT community, as these groups are currently under-represented in our organisation.
Job Summary 
The Volunteer Coordinator will lead the development, recruitment, coordination and support of volunteers across NDADA. The postholder will help ensure that volunteers have a positive, rewarding and well-supported experience while making a meaningful contribution to the organisation's work supporting people affected by domestic abuse.
The role will involve recruiting, inducting, training and supporting volunteers across a range of services and activities, including administration, gateway, fundraising, events, community engagement, counselling support and other organisational functions. The postholder will work closely with managers and staff to identify volunteer opportunities, ensure volunteers are safely integrated into services and maintain effective volunteer systems and records.
A key part of the role will be promoting volunteering opportunities within local communities, developing relationships with local organisations, educational providers and community groups, and helping NDADA increase community involvement in its work.
This postholder would spread their hours evenly between NDADA and Temperance House, North Devon's Women's Centre. Temperance House is currently being developed, and we have volunteers keen to support with the development. The Sustainability Coordinator supports the delivery and advancement of sustainable practices across Phoenix ME’s projects and operations. This role involves developing a broad understanding of key sustainability principles, including green certifications, embodied carbon, waste, energy, and responsible sourcing. The Sustainability Coordinator will contribute to both project-specific outcomes and wider business initiatives, promoting innovation and helping to position Phoenix ME as an industry leader in climate action and sustainability.
Key responsibilities:
Support project teams in meeting sustainability objectives, ensuring compliance with legal, client, and internal sustainability requirements throughout the project lifecycle.
Assist in the development and implementation of project-specific carbon and sustainability strategies, including setting and tracking measurable outcomes.
Contribute to the delivery of purpose-led and measurable sustainability outcomes on projects, aligned with client expectations and Company sustainability goals.
Collect and verify sustainability data from suppliers, subcontractors, and project teams to support internal reporting and client submissions.
Support embodied carbon assessments for MEP systems, including data gathering and analysis using relevant tools and methodologies.
Create and analyse thermal models, calculating operational energy consumption for projects where required.
Conduct research into client sustainability requirements and tailor approaches to align with project-specific goals and requirements.
Conduct research into emerging sustainability trends, client requirements, and industry best practices to support continuous improvement and innovation within the business.
Assist the SLT with understanding and shaping Phoenix ME’s internal ESG strategy.
Please note this is a full time in office position based in London. Transport to and from the office will be included on top of salary.

jobs.details_text:
Product Compliance & Sustainability Coordinator | Fashion Retailer | London 
About the Role 
We're working with an established fashion retailer looking for a Product Compliance & Sustainability Coordinator to support its technical, environmental and ethical sourcing standards across the business.
This is a varied role combining product compliance, regulatory research, supplier engagement and sustainability initiatives. You'll play an important part in ensuring products, materials and packaging meet relevant UK and EU requirements, while helping the business improve supply chain transparency and prepare for evolving legislation.
It's a great opportunity for someone with a background in product compliance or sustainability who enjoys taking ownership and working in a fast-paced fashion environment.
Key Responsibilities 
Monitor UK and EU product, chemical, packaging and labelling regulations, ensuring relevant standards are met across the product lifecycle.
Coordinate supplier documentation, declarations and technical records, maintaining accurate compliance databases and reporting information.
Identify compliance risks and work with suppliers to resolve issues and implement corrective actions.
Support ethical sourcing, factory audits and supply chain standards.
Research sustainable materials, packaging solutions and relevant industry certifications.
Monitor emerging legislation and support future requirements around product traceability.
Work cross-functionally with Buying, Design, Production and other teams to communicate regulatory updates, promote best practice and ensure product claims are accurate and substantiated.
About You 
Previous experience in product compliance, sustainability, garment technology or a related field, ideally within fashion or retail.
Knowledge of UK and EU regulations, particularly chemical restrictions, packaging and environmental compliance.
A genuine interest in sustainability and responsible sourcing.
Strong Excel, data management and organisational skills, with excellent attention to detail.
Confident communicator, comfortable working with suppliers and multiple internal stakeholders.
Proactive and solutions-focused, able to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.

This role is required to work with vulnerable groups including children and any offer of employment or volunteering is subject to a satisfactory enhanced DBS check.

Duration: Permanent

Interview dates: TBC
For this role, you’ll need to complete our online assessment instead of using a C.V. or online application form. This will help us understand more about your strengths and give you more information on the role. 
What it's like to work here Working within a wonderful, bustling atmosphere this role of Community, Participation & Volunteering Assistant, will support with operations and the organisation of community events and activities. Together with a team of volunteers you will provide a fantastic welcome to Osterley Park and House. You’ll connect with people and help them connect with nature through outdoor activities, especially Cycle Hire and outdoor walks/running groups, while also raising awareness of our work for climate action. 
What you'll be doing As our Community, Participation & Volunteering Assistant, you'll be supporting the wider team by maintaining links with the local community. You’ll help to make this a flexible, positive and inclusive place for partners, community groups and volunteers to get involved. This will mean supporting established community-led events, such as for Eid and Diwali.
You’ll support our work in developing new ways of working together and deepening relationships with existing and new audiences. You’ll also support our teams in offering a warm welcome and working with all kinds of people. 
You'll be based in Osterley Park and House and may also help off-site by going into community spaces. Working alongside our community partners, you'll help with day-to-day operations while welcoming visitors, helping ensure that they have a safe and enjoyable visit. 
You'll support the Active Outdoors Assistant by covering Cycle Hire during periods of annual leave, and assist the running of this service on weekends when required. You will assist with the organisation of volunteers and may help with some practical maintenance tasks (full training and resources provided - particularly for Cycle Hire). 
You'll support the Senior Community, Participation and Volunteering Manager with administration tasks relating to community visits and events.

focused on giving great service to everyone you meet 
a team player, but also happy to work on your own initiative

jobs.details_text:
Our client, a media publishing company, is seeking to appoint a Campaign Reporting Executive to take responsibility for producing accurate, timely and client-ready reports on the performance of client campaigns.
Reporting to the Managing Director and working closely with Projects, Marketing and Account Management teams, the successful candidate will use data from a variety of internal reporting tools to validate campaign results, produce Excel and PowerPoint reports, and respond credibly to follow-up questions from internal teams and clients. The successful candidate will also be comfortable communicating with clients when needed and be looking to develop into a more senior role in the future.
We are looking for an ambitious and analytical graduate with previous experience in reporting, data management, business intelligence support or similar with excellent Excel and PowerPoint skills.
This is a hybrid role (2 days in and 3 from home) and is based in Bourne End. 
Responsibilities 
Produce accurate, timely and well-presented client campaign reports, primarily in PowerPoint and Excel.
Extract and review data from Power BI and relevant internal systems, checking completeness, consistency and accuracy before reporting.
Report on live webinars, on-demand content, email, social and other campaign activity, as required.
Analyse performance measures including registrations, attendance, on-demand views, engagement, viewing duration and campaign conversion.
Analyse audience demographics including geography, job title, specialty and areas of interest, where available and appropriate.
Create clear tables, charts, and supporting commentary (where required).
Work to agreed reporting templates, deadlines and quality-control processes, maintaining consistent presentation and terminology.
Answer internal and occasional client questions about reported results, explaining the data clearly and credibly.
Maintain organised source data, calculations, report versions and approval records.
Identify recurring reporting issues and recommend practical improvements to data quality, templates and workflows.
Skills and Experience 
Around 2+ years' experience in reporting, data management, business intelligence support or a comparable role.
Strong numerical and analytical skills, with the ability to identify inconsistencies and interrogate results.
Advanced working knowledge of Excel, including organising, checking and presenting data in clear charts and tables.
Experience using Power BI reports or dashboards to retrieve, interrogate and interpret data.
Good PowerPoint skills and the ability to turn data into a polished, concise client-facing report.
Excellent attention to detail and a methodical, exact approach to quality control.
Clear written and verbal communication, including the confidence to explain performance data to non-technical colleagues and clients.
The ability to manage several reporting deadlines and prioritise work without compromising accuracy.
Qualified to degree level or equivalent. A numerical, analytical, agency or wider business background is desirable, although not essential.
Please note that we will only contact those candidates that we assess as suitable for the positions we have currently available based on their experience, training, and skills. If we do not have anything suitable, we will not keep your CV for more than 30 days.

We aspire to have a diverse and inclusive workplace and strongly encourage suitably qualified applicants from a wide range of backgrounds to apply.

jobs.details_text:
Videographer & Editor – TCG 
Salary + Benefits + Bonus + Stock Option Plan
Most card grading happens out of sight. A card goes in the post, a number comes back, and nobody sees what happened in between. We want people to see all of it.
Our grading happens under forensic imaging instruments, the same kind border forces use to catch forged passports, and covers cards from eleven games: Pokémon, One Piece, Disney Lorcana, Yu-Gi-Oh!, Digimon, Union Arena, Magic: The Gathering, Gundam Card Game, Dragon Ball Super Card Game, Dragon Ball Super Fusion World and Riftbound. We measure. We don't eyeball.
We are establishing a new laboratory with serious equipment and a grading scale that runs to 1,000 points, because ten was never enough. We are looking for a videographer and editor to bring it to the screen: someone who shoots it, cuts it and finishes it, and the sort of person who can make a corner measurement as watchable as a pack opening.
What we actually do A card arrives. It is photographed under visible, ultraviolet and infrared light, measured to a hundredth of a millimetre, and assessed across twelve axes: six scored, and six inspected and verified, all approved by AEL lab technicians. Along the way we establish whether it has been trimmed, rebuilt or faked.
Mycroft.AI, our grading intelligence, turns the measurements into a score. A human confirms it. The card is then sealed in a tamper-evident case with an NFC chip and returned to its owner with a certificate and a permanent registry record.
Every step of that is worth watching. You would be the one holding the camera, and the one deciding what makes the cut.
What you'll do 
Film the laboratory at work: cards under ultraviolet and infrared light, measurements coming up on screen, the instruments and the people running them.
Shoot the moments collectors wait for: the grade reveal, the case being sealed, and the NFC tap that brings up a card's registry record.
Edit what you shoot for @AELgrading on YouTube, TikTok and Instagram: quick-turnaround short-form for Shorts, Reels and TikTok, and finished long-form for YouTube, working to briefs from our Head of Content.
Finish every piece properly: colour grade, sound mix, captions, titles and simple motion graphics, exported in the right format for each platform.
Turn the science into something anyone can follow: how centering is measured, what a trimmed card looks like, why a fake fails.
Cover card shows, shop events and creator collaborations, travelling when the story is somewhere else.
Shoot stills when the job calls for it: cases, cards, the laboratory and the team, for the website and our channels.
Run the kit and the edit library: cameras, lenses, lighting and audio in working order; every project and file named, versioned and backed up; music and footage properly licensed. A clip you can't find is a clip you didn't shoot.
Work within the laboratory's security and publishing rules. Some things are never filmed, and nothing is published without sign-off from our marketing team.
Who you are
A videographer and editor with a portfolio to prove it: you can shoot, light and record clean sound, then cut it into something people watch to the end.
Strong TCG knowledge and keen to own the process: you know why a card matters before you point a camera at it.
Good at macro and product work. If you can film a holo card without a stripe of glare across it, we want to see it.
Fluent in Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve or Final Cut Pro, confident grading colour and mixing sound, and comfortable building titles and motion graphics. After Effects is a plus.
You edit for the viewer: a strong hook, good pacing, and nothing in the cut that hasn't earned its place.
You know what works on YouTube, TikTok and Instagram in the card world: vertical and horizontal, thirty seconds and thirty minutes.
Comfortable directing people on camera, from a grader at the bench to a visiting creator.
Detail-obsessed. Not in the CV sense, but in the sense that a fingerprint on a case or a reflection in the shot bothers you.
Full training is provided on the laboratory, its systems and our filming and security procedures.
Team player, with multiple opportunities for growth; able to hold conversations, dive into other roles to help colleagues out and have fun doing so.
A grading background is not essential as long as you're into detail and a TCG enthusiast. Ideal for outgoing, creative individuals who are into being part of something fun and industry leading.
What it's like A new laboratory opening its doors this autumn, and a brand being built in public. You will help decide how AEL looks on screen, and the look you set is the one every video after you follows.
This role is designed for motivated individuals eager to apply their TCG and creative skills in a specialised field that combines craftsmanship with technology. Join us to be part of a passionate team dedicated to excellence in trading card grading!
We also have an environment of some really cool things coming down the pipeline and would love a community enthusiast to come on this journey with us.
Please include a link to your showreel or portfolio with your application, and tell us which pieces you shot and which you edited. We would rather see your work than read about it.

You will collaborate with various departments, including Product, Marketing, UX, and Newsroom Capabilities, to track key performance indicators and provide insights to aid business decisions. Your responsibilities will include analysing data, identifying trends, and making recommendations to enhance customer engagement, acquisition and retention.

The opportunity to work in a friendly but highly motivated and collaborative in-house team, which is independent and highly agile.
Your opinion will always be sought and listened to.
An opportunity to grow and learn from working with us and the wider business.
Competitive salary.
Flexible working with the opportunity to primarily work remotely; office days will be in the London office. 
Key Responsibilities 
You will collaborate with the reader revenue team to track key performance indicators, including building required reports and visualisations.
You will proactively identify trends in metrics and deep-dive into areas of concern/opportunity.
You will conduct analyses of subscriber churn trends across various cohorts, focusing on opportunities to increase lifetime value.
You will work closely with our marketing team to champion campaign effectiveness, including valuable A/B tests to enhance performance.
You will work with the wider analytics team to help develop our customer journey mapping and conversion attribution. Analyse and connect various customer touchpoints to guide effective strategies for conversion and retention.
You will assist the head of newsletters with monitoring and tracking key performance metrics, generating reports to provide insights for product and editorial changes, and identifying opportunities for new newsletter products.
You will help analyse app user data, lifetime value of in-app subscribers, churn levels and conversion rates to identify trends and make recommendations for improvement.
You will communicate the results of analysis to stakeholders, highlighting issues and making recommendations.

Expert knowledge and skills in using Power BI, Microsoft Excel , and other relevant business intelligence tools.
Strong knowledge of key analytical tools & languages ( SQL, Adobe, Google, Data Studio, Python) 
Proven analysis and insight experience using relevant tools and methods to source and analyse data from multiple sources.

Strong planning and organisational skills to manage multiple tasks and deliver reliable analysis and reports to deadline.
The skills to communicate effectively to all key stakeholders clearly, confidently and concisely.
A proactive approach and a curious mindset.
Drive to grow, develop and succeed professionally.
Excellent attention to detail.

Turn research, insight, data, policy and member activity into accessible, accurate communications for members, prospective members, media and other audiences.
Identify stories, case studies, evidence and content angles; support the Communications Manager and PR agency with research-led and member stories.
Plan and deliver communications activity around research, insight, impact and policy outputs.
Write and deliver the monthly u3a Friends newsletter and other Trust newsletters.
Contribute to organic social media and work with Digital Marketing to improve content, messaging and calls to action using performance insights.
Ensure publications, reports and publicity materials are clear, accessible and consistent with u3a’s brand.
Use CMS, email/e-CRM, social platforms and Adobe Creative Suite/Canva or similar tools to produce content.
Build strong relationships with staff, volunteers, members, trustees, suppliers and external partners; support other departmental projects as needed.

Experience in communications, content, marketing or research communications, creating material for different audiences across web, newsletters, email, social media, reports, publications or PR.
Ability to identify strong stories and work with colleagues and stakeholders to turn them into content.
Strong editorial judgement, writing, editing and proofreading, with excellent attention to detail.
Able to translate complex research, insight, data and evidence into clear, engaging, accurate and accessible communications.
Skilled in digital content creation, prioritising multiple projects and deadlines, and building constructive working relationships.
Understanding of audience-focused communication, brand consistency, accessibility, inclusion and the use of research and evidence in PR and engagement.
Familiarity with CMS, email and social media tools and Adobe Creative Suite or similar. A marketing or communications qualification is advantageous; equivalent experience is accepted.
Creative, curious, collaborative and proactive; sound judgement, care with evidence, flexibility and a commitment to presenting u3a as active, relevant and welcoming.
Desirable 
Experience in a charity, membership organisation, public sector or education setting.
Experience creating infographics, animations, images or short-form video, including editing.
Experience using Mailchimp or similar email platforms, Joomla or another CMS, and channel performance data to improve content.
Knowledge of lifelong learning, volunteering, community participation, positive ageing and the age agenda.
First six months 
Learn the Trust’s content tools and build relationships across Marketing, Communications, Digital Marketing, Policy and Research.
Connect research and policy with communications, translating insight into compelling, accurate content.
Use performance data to improve messages and calls to action, newsletters, web, social, PR and publications.
Make better use of research and impact evidence to support awareness, engagement and membership growth.
How to apply Please submit your CV and a cover letter outlining how your skills and experience match the job description. In your letter, include a short answer to each question:

3. This role will work closely with members and u3as to find engaging stories. How do you build strong working relationships, and get people talking?

jobs.details_text:
Job Introduction 
At Turning Point we provide services across the whole country which delivers end to end drug and alcohol treatment and support, family services, housing advice and support for those in contact with the criminal justice system, needle exchange system, and custody outreach. We are a specialist in delivering whole treatment system approaches across cities and county areas, which has led to the reduction in people falling through gaps between services and delivers improved outcomes. 
An exciting opportunity has arisen to join Horizons, a vibrant new partnership delivering substance use treatment and recovery services in Bristol. Horizons is delivered in partnership between Turning Point, Bristol Drugs Project, and seven other local and national partners. The partnership combines Turning Point’s experience as an outstanding national substance use provider together with Bristol Drugs Project’s long history of excellent service delivery in the city.
As a Drug and Alcohol Recovery Worker based in our Homelessness team, and working at our Central Bristol, you'll make a real difference in the community and to their lives as you develop the personal, flexible and realistic support packages they need to help turn things around. 
The salary scale for our Recovery Worker roles is between £25,870 - £30,265. See our full salary scale below. Starting salary will be dependant on experience with annual pay progression up to scale point 
1 £25,870 2 £26,905 3 £27,981 4 £29,101 5 £30,265 You will have opportunities to progress your career with a structured learning journey and clearly defined career pathways that will enable you to achieve your long-term goals and work to your strengths.
Whether you are looking to progress into a management and leadership role or to be a specialist in your field as an Advanced Substance Use Practitioner at Turning point we will support and encourage you on your career journey.
Role Responsibility 
The successful candidate will support the Homelessness Team in taking a hands-on approach to reducing drug related harm in Bristol. This will include managing a case load of clients seeking harm reduction advice, Opiate Substitution Therapy (OST) and/or Tier 4 (in-patient) treatment.
You will spend much of your time working alongside key partners so the ability to manage relationships with housing services, primary care and mental health services, are essential. 
The successful candidate will work in partnership with the wider Bristol Horizons teams in delivering the ambitions of the Horizons service. To do this you must be organised, resilient, focused, able to work in a team or independently, have good communication skills, and be innovative in your approach. 
As well as the responsibility of having a case load, your regular duties will include: 
Providing harm reduction interventions such as Naloxone, needle exchange and Blood Bourne Virus (BBV) Testing 
Street Outreach 
Hostel Inreach 
This is an exciting opportunity for the right candidate to play an integral role in a new and developing service.
The Ideal Candidate 
Having handled a significant caseload in a busy environment as a Recovery Worker, Outreach Worker or similar, you'll have a deep understanding of substance use and homelessness. It's an extremely varied role, so flexibility and knowledge of relapse and other barriers to treatment will be vital. 
Completing assessments with new service users, delivering key working sessions, compiling risk assessments and risk management plans, care planning and reduction plans are just some of the varied duties you will be providing. 
Excellent IT skills with knowledge of Word, Excel, and Outlook etc. are essential for this role. Holding a full driving licence and having access to a car is desirable. 
About us 
As a leading health and social care provider with more than 300 locations across England, we take real pride in the services we offer.
We run all of our services on a not-for-profit basis; instead, we invest every penny back into our services and people. We never stop believing in change for the better, and we work constantly to improve the lives of the people we support.
What Benefits Will I Receive? 
We know reward looks different to each person and so whether its ways to make your money go further, a culture supporting recognition and celebration, or opportunities to boost your career – we want to support you in every way we can with our total reward package:
25 days’ paid holiday a year + Bank Holidays, increasing with each year of service up to 27 days + Bank Holidays. Plus the option to buy additional holidays and spread the cost.
Join our team and discover the comprehensive benefits we offer by following this link to explore all the exciting perks available to our employees. Turning Point Benefits
We reserve the right to close this advert early if we are able to appoint to the vacancy before the advertised closing date.
Turning Point

jobs.title: Commercial Analyst
jobs.details_text:
Music is Universal
It’s the passionate and dedicated team at Universal Music who help make us the world’s leading music company. From A&R to finance, legal to digital, sales to marketing, Universal Music is the place to grow and develop your career within a truly commercial and innovative business that leads in everything it does.
Everyone is welcome to apply for our roles, and we are determined to ensure that no applicant or employee receives less favourable treatment because of gender, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion, belief, age, marital status, background, pregnancy, or caring responsibilities. We also recognise the importance of diversity of thought within our teams and are fully committed to embracing the talents of people with autism, dyslexia, ADHD, and other forms of neurocognitive variation.
We will always seek to make appropriate adjustments to recruitment, workplaces, and work processes to be fully inclusive to people with different needs and working styles. If you need us to make any reasonable adjustments for you from application onwards, including alternatives to the online form or to disclose a neurocognitive condition, please email UniversalMusicCareers@umusic.com. 
The A Side: A Day in The Life 
The successful candidate will join a team delivering commercial analysis and operational support across UMG’s global business. This role combines structured process ownership with analytical responsibilities, supporting revenue operations, reporting, and stakeholder insights.
You will work with large-scale datasets from leading global technology platforms, alongside label revenue reconciliation for major artists including K-pop acts such as BTS and Stray Kids. The role involves delivering bespoke analysis for a wide range of stakeholders and building reporting tools (e.g., dashboards) to track performance, identify anomalies, and explain changes in revenue, user behaviour, and market trends.
In addition, you will support deal-specific recharge and rebill activities, requiring a self-motivated, detail-oriented problem solver who can collaborate with colleagues across UMG’s global network to resolve time-sensitive queries. The ideal candidate is a self-starter with strong intuition, capable of working independently and taking ownership without the need for close supervision.
The role includes regular stakeholder interaction, translating complex analysis into clear, concise commercial insights, and supporting both recurring processes and ad hoc requests in a fast-paced environment.
The B Side: Skills & Experience 
• Analyse revenue, user, and market trends, identifying anomalies and key drivers
• Own and manage label revenue recharge processes , including validation, market follow-ups, and issue resolution leveraging automation techniques
• Support deal-specific recharge and rebill activity , applying knowledge of distribution agreements
• Build dashboards, data visualisations and reporting tools for monitoring commercial and operational performance
• Investigate data issues and explain performance changes clearly to stakeholders
• Deliver ad-hoc analysis and stakeholder-ready outputs with clear commentary and insight
• Communicate effectively, simplifying complex data for non-technical audiences
Person Specification 
Necessary 
• Degree or equivalent experience in a relevant field (business, finance, data, etc.)
• Strong analytical skills with high attention to detail and a problem-solving mindset
• Experience with SQL, BigQuery, Python, Excel, and/or similar tools
• Strong automation skills using SQL + Python and related cloud platforms
• Experience in reporting, analytics, or commercial/finance operations
• Ability to manage multiple workstreams and deadlines
• Strong communication skills, with the ability to turn data into clear insights
Desirable 
• Experience with dashboarding/BI tools
• Familiarity with data pipelines and reporting structures
• Experience producing presentation-ready analysis and materials
• Exposure to music, media, or entertainment industry data
Just So You Know…
The company presents this job description as a guide to the major areas and duties for which the jobholder is accountable. However, the business operates in an environment that demands change and the jobholder's specific responsibilities and activities will vary and develop. Therefore, the job description should be seen as indicative and not as a permanent, definitive, and exhaustive statement.

jobs.details_text:
About the Business 
Quilter plc is a leading wealth management business, helping to enable brighter financial futures for every generation. 
Quilter oversees £157.4 billion in customer investments (as of August 2026). It has an adviser and customer offering spanning financial advice, investment platforms, multi-asset investment solutions, and discretionary fund management. The business is comprised of two segments: Affluent and High Net Worth. 
Affluent encompasses the financial planning business, Quilter Financial Planning, the Quilter Investment Platform and Quilter Investors, the multi-asset investment solutions business. 
High Net Worth includes the discretionary fund management business, Quilter Cheviot, together with Quilter Cheviot Financial Planning - offering a highly personalised service to private clients, charities, trustees, and professional partners. Quilter Cheviot has presence throughout the UK, Ireland and Channel Islands. 
At Quilter we never stand still. Our foundations are rooted in our extraordinary expertise, which is trusted by hundreds of thousands of customers, but we have great ambitions to stay one step ahead and make an even greater difference to the people and communities we serve, including our colleagues. 
Our business is transforming, becoming AI-enabled, and even more customer centric. This goes for our internal communications team too. So, if you want to be bold in the pursuit of big ambitions, bring new ideas, and challenge and evolve what we do, it's the perfect time to join us!
About the Role 
Level: 4
Department: HR & Communications
Location: Southampton, United Kingdom (Preferred location) or London, United Kingdom (Hybrid working)
Contract Type: Fixed Term Contract
Contract Length: 12 months
Regulated/Non-Regulated: Non-Regulated
The Internal Communications Manager - Channels, Content and Data leads the: 
Strategy, management and evolution of Quilter's internal communications channels , ensuring colleagues can easily discover, understand and act on information that supports the organisation's strategy, culture and employee experience.
Quality, planning and effectiveness of internal communications content , setting high editorial standards and working with Internal Communications Business Partners to ensure content is engaging, accessible, targeted and aligned to Quilter's strategic priorities.
Data, insight and measurement of internal communications , using audience, content and channel data to generate actionable insight, improve targeting and continually increase communications effectiveness and engagement.
AI-enabled evolution of our channels, content and ways of working , identifying and applying opportunities to improve colleague experience, communications quality, team productivity and the service we provide.
Since IC is part of the HR function, the Internal Communications Manager - Channels, Content and Data, will be deeply connected to Quilter's people strategy and will constantly look for opportunities to build connection and create alignment across the function.
Key Responsibilities 
Channel Management 
Lead the strategy, management and ongoing development of Quilter's internal communications channels, ensuring they meet evolving colleague and business needs.
Continually evolve Quilter's channels to maximise AI and technology opportunities, improving the colleague experience and making information easier to discover, understand and act on.
Identify and implement channel improvements, bringing new thinking and external best practice to improve communications effectiveness.
Work closely with relevant teams across Quilter to ensure our internal communications channels remain effective, accessible and fit for purpose.
Use insight and performance data to continually optimise the role, purpose and effectiveness of individual channels and the overall channel mix.
Content Management & Quality 
Set and maintain high editorial and content standards across internal communications, ensuring communications are clear, engaging, accessible and aligned to Quilter's strategic priorities.
Lead content planning and coordination across IC channels, working closely with Internal Communications Business Partners to ensure colleagues receive relevant communications at the right time and through the right channels. Develop effective IC campaigns.
Provide editorial oversight and quality assurance for key organisational communications, continually raising standards and ensuring consistency of tone, messaging and presentation.
Use audience insight and performance data to understand which content, formats and approaches are most effective, applying those insights to continually improve content.
Explore and embed appropriate uses of AI in content creation and management, improving quality, creativity, personalisation and productivity.
Data, Insight & Measurement 
Develop and own an internal communications measurement framework, establishing meaningful measures of success across channels, content and campaigns.
Proactively use data to provide a clear and consistent view of communications performance and colleague engagement. identifying which audiences, content, channels, formats and approaches are most effective and translating this into recommendations for the IC team.
Lead the use of audience data, segmentation and targeting to make communications increasingly relevant and effective.
Track trends over time, identifying changes in colleague behaviour and engagement and using these insights to continually refine channel and content strategies.
Leverage AI and technology to improve communications measurement, analysis and insight.
Communications Delivery 
Play a central role in delivering high-profile communication moments, including Quilter Conferences and Financial Results. 
Oversee publication of regular communication outputs such as fortnightly e-newsletter, regular cadence of leadership messaging, people cycle messages and business-as-usual updates.

jobs.details_text:
We are recruiting a Community Engagement Officer on behalf of a respected professional membership organisation.
This is an excellent opportunity for an organised, personable and proactive individual to join a busy membership and engagement team, supporting professional communities, committees, working groups and a varied programme of events and educational initiatives.
The successful candidate will enjoy building relationships, facilitating online communities and ensuring the smooth coordination and delivery of membership activities, webinars and events.
The Role 
Reporting to the Head of Membership & Engagement, you will provide operational and administrative support across the organisation's committees, working groups, membership communities and programmes.
Working closely with colleagues and volunteer groups, your responsibilities will include:
Supporting and coordinating committees, working groups and membership communities, including meeting arrangements, agendas, minute-taking, correspondence and action tracking.
Managing and moderating online membership communities, welcoming new participants, encouraging discussion and ensuring content is appropriate and engaging.
Acting as a first point of contact for event and webinar enquiries, managing shared inboxes and responding to member and delegate queries.
Supporting the end-to-end administration and logistical delivery of webinars and events, including platform setup, speaker liaison, presentation management and live event support.
Managing post-event feedback surveys, CPD certificates and delegate communications.
Maintaining event calendars, trackers and relevant website information, ensuring details are accurate and up to date.
Providing administrative and logistical support for educational programmes, accreditation schemes and other membership initiatives.
Supporting grant administration, member surveys and other organisational projects.
Identifying opportunities to improve administrative processes, member communications and the overall experience for volunteers and members.
Supporting the organisation at conferences and events as required.
We are seeking an experienced administrator or membership professional with excellent organisational, communication and relationship management skills.
You will ideally have:
Experience in online community management or moderation, such as professional forums, membership platforms or online groups.
A proven background in administration, ideally within a membership, events, committee, community or programme support environment.
Strong customer service skills, including experience managing shared inboxes and responding to enquiries professionally and efficiently.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including accurate minute-taking, proofreading and correspondence.
Strong attention to detail and the ability to manage several priorities and deadlines simultaneously.
The confidence to build relationships with senior professionals, volunteers and a diverse membership community.
Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office, and the ability to learn new digital systems quickly.
Basic experience updating website content through a CMS and supporting online event promotion.
An understanding of GDPR and good data management practices.
Experience of supporting committees and working groups, administering webinars or coordinating events would be advantageous. Experience within a professional body, learned society or membership organisation would also be beneficial.
Familiarity with platforms such as Discourse, Freshdesk, Typeform, Canva or Kentico would be useful, although experience with equivalent systems will be considered.
You will be a self-starter with a flexible and adaptable approach, able to manage a varied workload independently while working collaboratively with colleagues and volunteers.
You will be personable, enthusiastic and highly organised, with excellent communication skills and the confidence to identify opportunities to improve processes and member services.
This is a varied role offering the opportunity to make a real contribution to member engagement, community development and the delivery of a busy programme of professional activities.
This is a hybrid role, with 2 days a week based in their London office. 
Starting salary – 35K plus excellent benefits. 
Apply now for immediate consideration.

Job Summary
The Fundraising and Community Engagement Coordinator will support the development and delivery of fundraising, community engagement and awareness-raising activity across NDADA and the Devon Domestic Abuse Alliance. The postholder will help coordinate fundraising campaigns, community events, supporter engagement and volunteer involvement, contributing to increased awareness, community support and income generation.
Working closely with colleagues across communications, fundraising, volunteering and service delivery, the postholder will help ensure activities are well organised, promoted effectively and aligned with organisational priorities. Fundraising and Community Engagement

• Help coordinate fundraising campaigns, appeals and community fundraising initiatives.
• Develop and maintain positive relationships with supporters, local businesses, community groups and partner organisations.
• Identify opportunities to raise awareness of NDADA and DDAA services within local communities.
• Represent the organisation at community events, fundraising activities and awareness-raising opportunities as required.
• Support the monitoring and recording of fundraising activity, outcomes and community engagement.
Events and Awareness Raising 
• Coordinate practical arrangements for fundraising, awareness and community events.
• Work with colleagues to ensure events are promoted effectively and delivered safely.
• Support the development and distribution of promotional materials and event resources.
• Attend events, information stands and awareness-raising activities as required.
• Gather feedback and learning from events to support future planning.
Working with Communications 
• Work closely with the Communications Coordinator and Social Media Content Writer to promote fundraising campaigns, community activities and events. 
• Provide content, stories and information to support social media, website and promotional activity.
• Help ensure messaging is consistent with NDADA and DDAA values and priorities.
Volunteer Support 
• Work alongside the Volunteer Coordinator to support volunteer involvement in fundraising and community activities.
• Help coordinate volunteer attendance at events and awareness activities.
• Support the recruitment, engagement and recognition of volunteers involved in fundraising initiatives.
Recording and Administration 
• Maintain accurate records relating to fundraising activity, events, volunteers and supporter engagement.
• Support monitoring, reporting and administration associated with fundraising and community engagement work.
• Contribute information for funding reports, service reports and organisational monitoring where required.
General Responsibilities 
• Work in accordance with NDADA values, policies and procedures.
• Promote equality, diversity, inclusion and trauma-informed practice. 
• Participate in supervision, team meetings and training.
• Maintain confidentiality and comply with data protection requirements. 
• Undertake other duties appropriate to the role.
Practical Requirements 
• Ability to work flexibly within the agreed working pattern.
• Willingness to attend fundraising, community and awareness events, including occasional evenings and weekends.
• Ability to travel across Devon where required.
• Full driving licence and access to a vehicle desirable, particularly when transporting event materials and attending community events.
To Apply 
If you feel you are a suitable candidate and would like to work for North Devon Against Domestic Abuse, please do not hesitate to apply.

jobs.details_text:
We are looking for experienced Environmental Permitting Specialists whose primary purpose will be to ensure necessary Environmental Permits are in place and to provide technical advice on permitting to support our business activities. Thames Water is committed to improving our impact on the environment, and this role plays a vital part in ensuring the success of our Environmental Regulation obligations.
What you will be doing as Environmental Permitting Specialist 
This role involves overseeing ongoing applications including permit variations, submission of new applications, project management, liaising with the regulators and other teams in Thames Water, and ensuring timely and high-quality submissions. 
This is an excellent opportunity to join a small, experienced team working on high-impact permitting projects across a diverse portfolio. This role offers a unique chance to: 
Contribute to complex, high-value applications that directly influence operational delivery and regulatory relationships.
Gain exposure to a broad range of environmental permitting scenarios, ideal for developing your understanding of permitting and regulation.
Make a visible impact across the wider organisation.
If you're looking to grow your expertise in environmental permitting while working on meaningful projects that shape real-world outcomes, this could be the perfect next step for your career.
Location - Hybrid Reading with the option to work at any of our other sites 
What you should bring to the role 
Experience working with Environmental Permitting, ideally gained within waste water.
Experience or academic background in an environmental, regulatory or water industry-related discipline.
Excellent planning, organisation and communication skills, with the ability to negotiate and liaise effectively with stakeholders.
Strong technical writing skills, with the ability to write clear, structured technical documents and coordinate complex permit applications.
Strong analytical background and excellent IT literacy.
What’s in it for you? 
Offering between £46,565 - £58,000 per annum, depending on experience.
Annual Leave - 26 days holiday per year, increasing to 30 with the length of service. (Plus bank holidays) 
Performance-related pay is directly linked to company performance measures and targets.
Generous Pension Scheme through AON.
Personal Medical Assessments – Open to all once a year.
Access to lots of benefits to help you take care of your and your family’s health and well-being, and your finances – from annual health MOTs and access to physiotherapy and counselling, to Cycle to Work schemes, shopping vouchers and life assurance.
Find out more about our benefits and perks (Please note different T&Cs apply if on secondment)
Who are we? 
We’re the UK’s largest water and wastewater company, with more than 16 million customers relying on us every day to supply water for their taps and toilets. We want to build a better future for all, helping our customers, communities, people, and the planet to thrive. It’s a big job, and we’ve got a long way to go, so we need help from passionate and skilled people, committed to making a difference and getting us to where we want to be in the years and decades to come.
Learn more about our purpose and values.
Working at Thames Wate r 
Thames Water is a unique, rewarding, and diverse place to work, where every day you can make a difference, yet no day is the same. As part of our family, you’ll enjoy meaningful career opportunities, flexible working arrangements and excellent benefits.
If you’re looking for a sustainable and successful career where you can make a daily difference to millions of people’s lives while helping to protect the world of water for future generations, we’ll be here to support you every step of the way. Together, we can build a better future for our customers, our region, and our planet.
Real purpose, real support, real opportunities. Come and join the Thames Water family. Why choose us? Learn more.
We’re committed to being a great, diverse, and inclusive place to work. We welcome applications from everyone and want to ensure you feel supported throughout the recruitment process. If you need any adjustments, whether that’s extra time, accessible formats, or anything else, just let us know. We’re here to help and support.
When a crisis happens, we all rally around to support our customers. As part of Team Thames, you’ll have the opportunity to sign up to support our customers on the frontline as an ambassador. Full training will be given for what is undoubtedly an incredibly rewarding experience. It’s also a great opportunity to learn more about our business and meet colleagues.
Disclaimer: Due to the high volume of applications we receive, we may close the advert earlier than the advertised date, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible to avoid disappointment.

jobs.details_text:
Our organization is seeking content writers to create articles and blog posts on a variety of topics.
The rate of pay is $20 per 100 words (this comes out to approximately $100 per article or $50 per hour).
Some topics you may be asked to write about include the following (you can always turn down a topic if you do not feel comfortable writing about it, however if you have experience or expertise in a specific area, please let us know):
Health & beauty
Fitness
Home Decor
Fashion
Sports
Do it yourself
Finance
Legal
Medical
Family/Parenting
Relationships
Real Estate
Restaurants
Contracting (plumbing, pool building, remodeling, etc.)
These are just some of the more general industries and topics that we cover. 
Requirements : 
We ask that all work be completed using a word processor such as Microsoft Word or Open Office
A reliable internet connection and the ability to meet deadlines
Good communication skills and respond in a timely manner to editorial staff when they ask for updates on tasks, etc
Work well as a team member with the rest of our content management and editorial staff
Note : Applicants to this job signaled that accessing some writing tasks may require payment.

jobs.details_text:
Communications Executive – London / Chertsey (Flexible hybrid working) | Full-Time / Permanent 
Up to £40,000 + bonus and excellent benefits including healthcare, wellbeing support, 27 days' annual leave plus bank holidays, life insurance and more. 
We're looking for a proactive Communications Executive to join the Compass Group UK & Ireland team – a market-leading food and support services company, delivering exceptional experiences across workplaces, healthcare, education, defence and leisure sectors. In this exciting role you will play a key role in delivering engaging communications (both external and internal), PR activity and content across some of Compass Group UK&I's leading workplace and leisure catering brands. 
This is the chance to develop your communications career within a fast-paced commercial environment, creating impactful content, supporting brand reputation and helping colleagues stay connected across the business. If you're a strong storyteller with a passion for PR and communications, we'd love to hear from you.
We are Compass Group UK&I 
We’re the UK’s largest food and support services provider: the people behind the food, hospitality and services that brighten your day, make you smile and put a spring in your step. Operating in thousands of locations across the UK & Ireland, we provide expert catering, cleaning, and facilities management services to a range of clients and sectors across the country. In the UK and Ireland we’re tens of thousands of talented people providing tasty, well-cooked food and support services to improve the health and wellbeing of workers, school children, hospital patients, military and visitors to the nation’s major sports and cultural events.
Communications Executive – The role 
Support the delivery of integrated communications and PR plans across the Workplace & Leisure sector and its brands
Create, edit and coordinate content for internal communications platforms and other communication channels
Research and draft press releases, feature articles, award submissions, case studies and briefing materials
Collaborate with operational and brand teams to source engaging colleague, client and business stories
Support PR agencies and external partners by coordinating briefs, actions and reporting
Maintain communications calendars, content pipelines and project plans to ensure activity is delivered on time
Proofread and quality-check communications materials to ensure accuracy, consistency and brand alignment
Support events, campaigns and wider communications initiatives across the business
What we're looking for 
Experience in communications, public relations, marketing, journalism or a related field
Strong writing, editing and proofreading skills with the ability to tailor content for different audiences
Experience creating content for digital, internal communications or social channels
Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines
Strong communication and relationship-building skills with internal and external stakeholders
Passion for storytelling, brand reputation and employee engagement
Proactive, collaborative and adaptable approach to work
Interest in hospitality, workplace services or leisure industries would be a bonus!
What you'll get in return 
Competitive salary with bonus and full company benefits
27 days' annual leave plus bank holidays, your birthday off, and a holiday purchase scheme
Healthcare & wellbeing: Aviva Digicare, Medicash (dental, optical, therapy treatments)
Mental health support: 24/7 Employee Assistance Programme
Family benefits: Enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption leave, plus additional family-friendly benefits
Perks & discounts: Shopping, entertainment and travel discounts, 20% off Nuffield Health and 10% off PureGym memberships
Financial wellbeing: Pension scheme, Life Assurance and preferred rates on salary finance products
Development opportunities: Professional subscriptions, ongoing training and structured career pathways
Compass Group is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive.
