jobs.details_text:
Join a Growing Organisation Making a Difference
An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Communications Officer to join a purpose-driven organisation undergoing significant growth and expansion.
This organisation delivers nationally recognised programmes that support professionals working with children and families and is investing heavily in new initiatives, services and stakeholder engagement. As a result, they are seeking a creative and commercially minded communications professional to help drive awareness, engagement and impact through compelling content and storytelling.
The Opportunity
Reporting into the Communications & Marketing function, you will play a key role in delivering external communications activity across digital, social media, email and content channels.
This is a highly varied role offering significant creative ownership, the opportunity to shape social media strategy, and exposure to a wide range of internal and external stakeholders.
You'll be responsible for identifying stories, producing engaging content, supporting campaigns and helping the organisation strengthen its profile with existing and emerging audiences.
Key Responsibilities
Create engaging written, visual and video content across multiple channels.
Manage and develop social media activity, including content planning, scheduling and publishing.
Produce articles, case studies, blogs, interviews and stakeholder stories.
Support communications and marketing campaigns that promote programmes and organisational initiatives.
Conduct interviews and gather content from colleagues, programme participants and stakeholders.
Collaborate with teams across the organisation to identify opportunities for storytelling and engagement.
Monitor digital performance and provide insight using website, social media and email analytics.
Contribute to audience development, channel optimisation and communications planning.
About You
We're keen to hear from candidates who combine excellent writing ability with strong digital communications experience.
Essential Skills & Experience
Experience in a Communications Officer, Content Officer, Digital Communications, Marketing Communications or Social Media role.
Exceptional written communication, editing and proofreading skills.
Experience managing professional social media channels.
Strong content creation skills across a range of formats.
Ability to translate complex information into engaging, audience-focused content.
Experience building relationships with stakeholders and sourcing content from subject matter experts.
Excellent organisational and project management skills.
Desirable Skills
Video production and editing experience.
Photography and content capture skills.
Experience using Canva, Adobe Creative Suite or similar design platforms.
Email marketing experience.
Analytics experience, including social media and website performance reporting.
Experience working within charity, public sector, education, membership or purpose-led organisations.
Ideal Candidate Profile
This role would suit a Communications Officer, Content Executive, Digital Communications Executive, Social Media Executive, Marketing Communications Executive or Content Specialist seeking a position where quality writing, creative storytelling and audience engagement are at the heart of the role.
Please include a brief supporting statement along with your CV

jobs.details_text:
We are looking for a creative, commercially minded and hands-on Marketing Manager to lead and deliver the festival's overall marketing strategy.
Reporting to the Festival Manager, you will oversee all marketing activity, from campaign planning and digital marketing to social media, PR, CRM, partnerships and artist announcements.
You will be responsible for driving ticket sales, growing audience engagement and ensuring all campaigns are delivered creatively, on time and within budget.
Key Responsibilities: 
Develop and deliver the overall festival marketing strategy.
Lead and manage marketing campaigns across digital, social, PR and other relevant channels.
Oversee artist announcements, line-up campaigns and marketing assets.
Manage social media, website, app and digital content.
Develop and deliver CRM and email marketing campaigns.
Manage external agencies, suppliers and media partnerships.
Identify promotional opportunities and partnerships to drive ticket sales.
Manage the marketing budget, campaign reporting and KPIs.
Oversee onsite photography, filming and content creation.
Manage and support junior members of the marketing team.
Lead onsite marketing activity throughout the festival build, live event and breakdown.
You will ideally have: 
Proven marketing experience within the music, festival or live events industry.
Experience managing integrated marketing campaigns and driving ticket sales.
Strong knowledge of digital marketing, social media, CRM and performance marketing.
Experience managing agencies, suppliers and marketing budgets.
Excellent organisational, communication and project management skills.
Experience managing or developing junior team members.
Proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite, Microsoft Office and content creation tools such as CapCut.
A creative, proactive and hands-on approach, with exceptional attention to detail.
A genuine passion for live music, festivals and the wider entertainment industry.
Handle actively welcomes applicants from under-represented backgrounds - we pride ourselves on attracting the best talent for every opportunity through a commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion.

Supplies & Facilities

Good communication skills.

Friendly, proactive, and reliable.

Flexible 8-hour-per-week role.

Supportive and collaborative working environment.

jobs.details_text:
Video & Design Assistant – Degree Apprenticeship 
Passionate about video and looking to build a career in the creative industries? Earn a degree, gain hands-on experience and get paid while you learn 
Oasis Community Learning is looking for a creative Video & Design Assistant to join our National Communications & Marketing Team, combining a fully funded degree apprenticeship through university with real-world experience.
What will the role involve?
• Planning, organising, filming and editing high-quality videos from the initial idea through to the finished product.
• Working with our academies to capture stories that showcase our people, communities and impact.
• Creating engaging graphics, photography and visual content for our digital channels.
• Collaborating with colleagues and creative agency partners to strengthen the Oasis brand.
Who are we looking for? 
Someone with practical video production experience, a creative eye and a genuine passion for developing a career in video and digital content. Experience could come from freelance work, personal projects, social media or previous employment. A portfolio demonstrating creative ability is essential; professional industry experience isn't.
Whether building on existing skills or changing career direction, this is an opportunity to turn creative ambition into a profession.
Initially you will be employed full time in the role, commencing the University Apprenticeship in September 2027. 
Earn a degree while you work, develop your technical skills and build a portfolio of professional work alongside experienced communications colleagues.
Based in London, with travel to academies nationwide (2 – 3 academies per week)
Full-time, 37 hours per week
Salary: SCP 4 - £31668 - SCP 8 - £33513 plus Local Government Pension Scheme - (Please note, you will join on the entry point of SCP 4)
Ready to turn your passion into a career?
Apply now and discover where a degree apprenticeship with Oasis could take you. 
This vacancy requires submission of a cv with a portfolio/examples of your work. 
Oasis is committed to safeguarding children and young people. An enhanced DBS check is required.

jobs.details_text:
Job category: Professional Services.
The University of Surrey is a global community of ideas and people, dedicated to life-changing education and research. We are ambitious and have a bold vision of what we want to achieve - shaping ourselves into one of the best universities in the world, which we are achieving through the talents and endeavour of every employee. Our culture empowers people to achieve this aim and to collectively, and individually, make a real difference. 
The Role 
The Centre for Vision, Speech and Signal Processing (CVSSP) is seeking to recruit a Research Community Manager (Deaf Communities) to connect its research on AI for sign languages with the Deaf community. You will join an established research group within a highly rated research department, working alongside researchers, engineers and a project manager, with close links to Deaf community organisations, partner universities and industry.
The post sits within Professor Bowden's sign language research group at CVSSP, which leads a portfolio of collaborative projects developing AI for sign languages. These include SignGPT, a five-year EPSRC Programme Grant with the University of Oxford and University College London building tools to translate between spoken language and sign language video in both directions; UMCS, a UK and Japan collaboration developing real-time sign language translation in everyday conversation; and a Google.org-funded project reducing the cost of sign language translation through AI. The projects are committed to working with and for the Deaf community, and this new role will lead that work. 
You will build relationships with Deaf organisations and represent the projects at community events; run Deaf user groups and user evaluations of new technology; lead the recruitment of Deaf participants and co-ordinate data collection and recording sessions; and make the projects and their findings accessible through BSL videos, accessible materials and Deaf-facing social media. 
About You 
Fluent British Sign Language and an in-depth knowledge of Deaf culture and the UK Deaf community are essential, along with experience of community engagement with Deaf people. A degree is not required where candidates have significant relevant experience. The post is offered at 0.5 FTE for upto 2 years (up to Nov 2028) in the first instance. Deaf candidates are strongly encouraged to apply. BSL/English interpreters will be provided for interviews, and we welcome requests for any other adjustments.
How to Apply 
Please upload your CV and a covering letter on the University website, explaining how you meet the essential criteria in the job description.
Informal enquiries related to the project to Professor Richard Bowden by e-mail:r.bowden@surrey.ac.uk .
Closing Date: 23 Nov 2026
Area: Professional Services
Salary: £18,847 to £23,025 per annum pro rata (0.5 FTE)

jobs.details_text:
Music is Universal
It’s the passionate and dedicated team at Universal Music who help make us the world’s leading music company. From A&R to finance, legal to digital, sales to marketing, Universal Music is the place to grow and develop your career within a truly commercial and innovative business that leads in everything it does.
Everyone is welcome to apply for our roles, and we are determined to ensure that no applicant or employee receives less favourable treatment because of gender, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion, belief, age, marital status, background, pregnancy, or caring responsibilities. We also recognise the importance of diversity of thought within our teams and are fully committed to embracing the talents of people with autism, dyslexia, ADHD, and other forms of neurocognitive variation.
We will always seek to make appropriate adjustments to recruitment, workplaces, and work processes to be fully inclusive to people with different needs and working styles. If you need us to make any reasonable adjustments for you from application onwards, including alternatives to the online form or to disclose a neurocognitive condition, please email UniversalMusicCareers@umusic.com. 
Department Description 
Global Technology powers the digital ecosystem behind UMG/UMPG. We develop and support secure, scalable systems and platforms used by artists, songwriters, partners & employees worldwide, while championing innovation and cultivating a culture that embraces emerging technologies and continuous improvement. 
With a global footprint, the Universal Music Group Royalty and Copyright Product Team designs, develops, delivers and maintains a number of technical solutions to calculate royalty accountings in a timely and accurate manner to our valued artists. We’re also providing them with an extensive and detailed visibility of these earnings from various sources of digital income. 
The team continuously collaborates with our international business teams to deliver innovative solutions, support best practices and improve processes for a better royalty flow. 
The Role 
The primary purpose of the role will be to support one of UMG’s Royalty platform and act as a key liaison between the business teams, local users, the development team and other support functions. This will include triaging support tickets, coordinating resolution activities, maintaining clear communication with stakeholders, and supporting audit and compliance controls associated with the application. 
The i-series Support Systems Analyst will report to the Technical Product Owner, who is responsible for delivering the roadmap and associated projects aimed at enhancing and optimising one of UMG’s core royalty calculation systems with a user base across more than 45 countries. 
Key Responsibilities 
Be Support Focused 
Act as a first point of contact for support issues raised by local users of the royalty application and business teams. 
Review, categorise and prioritise tickets in ServiceNow and JIRA with the business team, ensuring clear ownership and status updates. 
Analyse reported issues to distinguish between user guidance, data or process issues, configuration queries, defects and enhancement requests. 
Work with the development team, QA team and local users to progress incidents and defects through resolution, retest and closure when required. 
Be Collaborative 
Build positive relationships with business stakeholders, local royalty teams and the application development team. 
Participate in regular meetings with stakeholders to review support demand, ticket trends, open risks and resolution progress.

Housing Interventions Worker 
Location: Gwent, Caerphilly, HMP Prescoed, HMP Usk, Torfaen (Pontypool)

Vacancy Type: Permanent
Want to make a real difference in preventing homelessness and helping people build a more stable future?
Join us as a Housing Interventions Worker, working full-time (35 hours per week) across Gwent. You’ll be based at Torfaen Probation Office in Pontypool, with travel to Caerphilly Probation Office, HMP Usk and HMP Prescoed, supporting men on probation and those preparing for release from custody to access safe, suitable accommodation.
What you’ll be doing

Sourcing suitable private rented accommodation, including shared houses, studios and one-bedroom properties.
Building relationships with landlords, letting agents, local authorities and housing providers.
Supporting clients with tenancy agreements, rent negotiations and referrals to specialist services.
Working with prison, probation and Camau colleagues to achieve positive outcomes and reduce reoffending.
Ensuring accommodation meets relevant safety standards and legal requirements.
What we’re looking for 
Good knowledge of housing and welfare benefits systems.
Experience providing housing, rehousing or welfare benefits advice.
Experience assessing adults with housing and wider support needs, including substance misuse.
Experience developing support plans to help people secure and maintain tenancies.
An understanding of homelessness, abstinence-based recovery and the challenges faced by people experiencing multiple disadvantages, including mental ill health, unemployment and substance use.
Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with a passion for helping people achieve lasting change.
If you’re passionate about tackling homelessness and helping people move towards a brighter future, we’d love to hear from you! 
All probation-based roles are subject to enhanced DBS checks and HMPPS security vetting. These checks can take up to 6-8 weeks to complete. Any offer of employment will be conditional upon the successful completion of both checks.

jobs.details_text:
About The Role
Why choose us? 
BRUSH Group provides the energy solutions that help power our built world . From power transformers to switchgear and engineering solutions, for generations, the BRUSH brand has stood for engineering excellence. 
We are committed to supporting the global effort for industrial decarbonisation and sustainable development and have set ambitious objectives to achieve our target of net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. 
What's the role? 
BRUSH Power Solutions is seeking a proactive and experienced Project Manager to lead the planning, coordination, and execution of HV electrical infrastructure projects across our new and existing developments across the South of England. 
Working Conditions - This role will be home based with expectations to visit our various substation sites across the south of england. 40hrs per week Monday - Friday. The ideal candidate should have a full UK drivers license and should be comfortable with travelling to various BRUSH sites as and when required as part of the role.Car allowance will be provided.
Key Responsibilities: 
Develop and implement project plans, schedules and budgets to ensure that projects are completed on time.
Identify and procure material, equipment and labour required for projects
Manage and coordinate the work of subcontractors and other vendors
Ensure projects are in compliance with all relevant laws, regulations and standards including Health and Safety regulations
Communicate with clients, stakeholders and regulatory agencies to ensure that project requirements are met and address any issues raised
Manage the quality of work and ensure that projects meet or exceed customer expectations
Identify and mitigate project risks, taking corrective action as needed
Maintain accurate project documentation and records
Manage the project financials, including forecasting, budgeting and cost management
Manage the project team, including assigning tasks and responsibilities, providing guidance and direction, and evaluating performance
Conducting regular project reviews and assessments to identify areas for improvement and implementing corrective actions
Continuously monitoring the project progress and ensure that the scope, time and cost are in line with the project plan and budget
Provide technical support and guidance to the project team members
Provide training to the team members to improve their technical and professional skills
Being up-to-date with the latest technologies, industry trends and best practices in project management
Maintain strong relationships with clients, stakeholders and regulatory agencies to ensure continued business opportunities
Manage the project aftercare process and ensure customer satisfaction
Manage internal and external stakeholder expectations by providing regular updates and progress reports
Continue to improve the project management process and methodologies including development and implantation of project management systems and procedures, to be more efficient and effective
What we’re looking for: 
HNC, Bachelor's or Master's degree in electrical engineering, or in electrical related discipline (or equivalent) is desirable. 
SMSTS or NEBOSH Health & Safety Management for Construction or IOSH Certificate in managing Health and Safety (or equivalent) is essential.
Project management certification, such as APMP from APM (desirable).
Skills 
Focused, self-motivated, and able to work both independently and collaboratively.
Strong ability to interpret complex requirements, assess risks, and communicate findings clearly.
Excellent organisational skills and time management skills with a strong ability to forward plan. 
Outstanding communication and interpersonal abilities, leadership, and organizational skills. 
Effective decision maker with the capability to work under pressure. 
Ability to coordinate site activities while maintaining high safety standards for all personnel. 
Strong understanding of commercial terms and conditions and their impact on project delivery.
Advantageous to have technical knowledge of HV/LV cable laying, switchgear installation, cable jointing and commissioning.
Proficient in use of MS office suite, including Excel and Microsoft Project.
Experience 
Proven experience in administering and delivering projects under NEC and FIDIC contract frameworks.
Demonstrated track record in leading complex projects using recognised project management methodologies, as well as applying electrical safety standards and regulations.
Experience in delivering projects that align with customer requirements and expectations.
Strong background in managing project budgets, including cost control and financial reporting.
Solid understanding of Health and Safety regulations, ensuring safe and compliant project execution. 
Significant experience in managing electrical power distribution projects, particularly in the energy or utility industry.
Ability to manage multiple stakeholders, including customers, contractors, and regulatory agencies
About The Organisation
BRUSH Power Solutions is able to deliver at every stage of a project’s lifecycle. From initial design and consultancy through to construction, testing, commissioning and connection, the team are on hand to provide comprehensive end-to-end HV infrastructure solutions for projects from 11kV to 400kV.
Along with the expertise BRUSH Power Solutions offers, our wider Power division also includes specialist ICP-accredited energy infrastructure contractor, McGowan Infrastructure. Often working in fragile and protected environments, the team utilise sustainable technologies to operate in way that minimises environmental impact, increasing biodiversity, and restores natural habitats.

jobs.details_text:
We are recruiting a Communications, Marketing & Digital Officer for a respected professional membership organisation.
This is an excellent opportunity for a creative, digitally confident communications professional to take ownership of a varied marketing and communications portfolio, helping to strengthen the organisation's brand, improve its digital presence and engage its membership community.
The successful candidate will enjoy combining creative content production with hands-on digital management, working across websites, email marketing, social media, video and promotional campaigns.
The Role 
Reporting to the Head of Membership & Engagement, you will play a key role in delivering the organisation's day-to-day communications, marketing and digital activity.
Working closely with colleagues across the membership, engagement and events teams, your responsibilities will include:
Planning, creating and publishing engaging content across the website, email communications and social media channels.
Managing and maintaining website content through a CMS, ensuring information is accurate, accessible and well structured.
Developing creative marketing materials, digital assets and campaign content for different audiences and initiatives.
Coordinating promotional campaigns for conferences, events, webinars and educational programmes.
Producing and editing video and multimedia content to support member communications and organisational campaigns.
Supporting the production of publications and other key creative projects, including editorial, design and publishing activity.
Monitoring digital engagement and campaign performance, using analytics and audience insight to identify opportunities for improvement.
Developing and maintaining reusable digital templates and creative assets.
Working with external digital, creative and media suppliers.
Supporting the organisation at conferences and events as required.
The Candidate 
We are seeking a proactive and creative communications and marketing professional with experience across digital channels and content production.
You will ideally have:
Proven experience in a communications, marketing or digital role, preferably within a membership organisation, charity or not-for-profit environment.
Experience managing website content through a CMS, including making structural and editorial improvements.
Excellent copywriting, creative writing, proofreading and editorial skills.
Experience using email marketing platforms and social media scheduling and analytics tools.
Practical video production and editing skills, with an understanding of engaging visual content.
Strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple deadlines and projects simultaneously.
An understanding of GDPR, digital accessibility and good data practices.
Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office, and the ability to pick up new digital platforms quickly.
Experience of marketing events, webinars or educational programmes would be advantageous, but is not essential, as would knowledge of Canva, Kentico CMS or Zoho CRM.
Personal Attributes 
You will be organised, enthusiastic and self-motivated, with the confidence to take ownership of projects and recommend improvements. Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work collaboratively with colleagues, external partners and volunteers are essential.
This is a varied role offering the opportunity to make a real contribution to an organisation's communications, digital development and member engagement.
This is a hybrid role with 2 days a week based in the London office. 
Starting salary circa -35K plus excellent benefits

Kingston College is looking for an experienced youth work professional to join our Student Services team as a Student Community Officer. jobs.details_text:
Are you passionate about supporting young people and creating a positive, inclusive College community? 
Kingston College is looking for an experienced youth work professional to join our Student Services team as a Student Community Officer. This is a varied, front-line role where you’ll build positive relationships with students, support those who may be considered ‘at risk’ or ‘hard to reach’, and help create an engaging, safe and welcoming environment across the College.
Working closely with Curriculum, Student Services and Security teams, you’ll maintain a visible and approachable presence across the College, engaging with students and signposting them to enrichment activities and appropriate support. You’ll lead and develop a programme of enrichment activities designed to increase student participation and strengthen the College community. You’ll recruit, coordinate and monitor engagement, identify opportunities to improve attendance and encourage students to get involved in activities and clubs.
A key part of the role will be providing early intervention and short-term one-to-one support to students who may be at risk of disengaging from education. You’ll also design and deliver targeted workshops covering areas such as conflict resolution, bullying and respect. You’ll work closely with internal teams and external partners to support safeguarding and student wellbeing, responding appropriately to challenging situations and using de-escalation, restorative and conflict-resolution approaches where necessary.
To be successful in this role, you’ll hold a Level 3 qualification or above in a relevant discipline, such as youth work, youth justice or social care, and have experience of working with young people in a school, College, youth or community setting. You’ll have experience of outreach, detached youth work or similar, with a good understanding of the issues that can affect a young person’s engagement, attendance and behaviour in education. You’ll also be able to lead on developing and adapting an Enrichment programme to meet student need and maintain attendance.
You’ll have a strong understanding of safeguarding and child protection, including contextual safeguarding, and experience of managing challenging behaviour using approaches such as de-escalation, negotiation and conflict resolution. An excellent communicator, you’ll be able to build positive relationships with young people while maintaining professional boundaries, work effectively with colleagues and external agencies, and confidently maintain accurate student records and written reports.
This role will be based at our Creative Industries Centre. 
Closing date for the return of completed applications is 25th November 2026 
The benefits package includes generous annual leave of 27 days plus up to 8 additional days over Christmas/New Year as well as an additional 5 days Wellbeing leave to enhance employees’ physical and mental health. There is an excellent pension scheme that receives a significant financial contribution from the employer (Teachers Pensions or Local Government Pension Scheme), subsidised sports facilities and professional development and training plus a salary sacrifice cycle to work scheme. The benefits package will be pro-rated for part time staff. 
South Thames Colleges Group is an equal opportunities employer and is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and vulnerable adults.
As outlined in the Public Sector Equality Duty of the Equality Act 2010, we are committed to equality of opportunity for all staff and applications from individuals are encouraged regardless of age, disability, sex, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief and marriage and civil partnerships.
As part of our due diligence checks on prospective employees, successful candidates will be subject to an enhanced DBS check, satisfactory references, an online search and proof of eligibility to work in the UK.
The South Thames Colleges Group is made up of Carshalton College, Kingston College, Merton College and South Thames College, which merged on 1 August 2017. South Thames Colleges Group is one of London’s largest providers of post-16 education and training and is an ongoing and significant contributor to its local communities. We aim to put students’ success at the heart of everything we do.
We are looking for hard-working and collaborative people who can join our team and help challenge our students to progress and achieve.

Communications Manager 
Based in Broxbourne, Hertfordshire
Permanent, full-time, 37 hours per week
Salary: £49,025 - £54,472
We’re looking for someone with ideas, diligence and drive to manage our Communications function. If you’re a marketing/communication professional with a keen sense of brand, quality and how to manage an organisation’s reputation, we can offer a role to get your teeth into.
In the role, you’ll manage a small team, helping them to create high-standard materials for all our key audiences. You’ll make sure our channels are maintained, events run well, tricky messages become engaging, and the organisation is supported to improve the way it communicates.
We need someone who knows how to keep a brand identity consistent, has an ear for the right words and an eye for visual design, and who can represent communications as a key function with confidence.
We’re looking for someone with… 
- Substantial experience in a communications role
- Knowledge of social housing and experience in an equivalent public sector and/or regulated industry
- An understanding of brand-setting principles and experience maintaining brand standards
- Experience planning and delivering events
- Experience using website content management systems and social media management tools
- Experience of media relations
- A relevant qualification in communication, press/journalism, marketing or a related discipline
You’ll also need a basic DBS check, which we’ll arrange and pay for.

We offer services designed to help our customers live comfortably in their homes, and we work to keep our buildings and estates maintained, offering support when money becomes an issue or when people get older. Our mission is to make a sustainable, positive change to the housing crisis for our customers and communities.

jobs.details_text:
Community Engagement Officer 
Oxted, Surrey | £29,000 FTE (pro rata) | 16 hours per week | 12-month fixed-term contract 
Are you an organised, personable and community-minded individual who enjoys bringing people together, building relationships and making a positive difference?
We are working with a well-established local charity to recruit a Community Engagement Officer to support an exciting community partnership initiative across East Surrey.
This is a fantastic opportunity for someone with experience in administration, event coordination and communications who would enjoy a varied role working with local charities, community groups and voluntary organisations.
The Opportunity 
Working as part of a small, supportive team, you will help connect local communities, organisations and services, ensuring that people's voices, experiences and priorities are heard.
This is a varied, hands-on position combining community engagement, administration, event organisation and communications. You will attend local meetings and forums, develop relationships with community organisations, help coordinate events and workshops, and support the delivery of newsletters, website updates and social media content.
The role is office-based in Oxted when not attending meetings or events, with regular travel throughout East Surrey.
Key Responsibilities 
Community Engagement & Relationship Building 
Attend community meetings, local forums and neighbourhood partnership events across East Surrey.
Build and maintain positive relationships with voluntary organisations, community groups and local partners.
Listen to local concerns, experiences and priorities, capturing key information and sharing insights with the wider partnership team.
Maintain accurate records of meetings attended, contacts made and issues raised.
Administration & Coordination 
Organise meetings, manage invitations, coordinate attendance and maintain diaries and schedules.
Keep contact databases, meeting notes, records and action logs up to date.
Respond to routine enquiries and provide general administrative and coordination support.
Liaise with partner organisations to support effective communication and day-to-day activities.
Events & Activities 
Assist with organising community events, workshops and partnership meetings.
Coordinate venues, bookings, invitations, refreshments and event materials.
Support event registration, on-the-day arrangements and post-event follow-up.
Communications & Social Media 
Help prepare and distribute newsletters and updates to community partners.
Draft short website articles, news items, event notices and community updates.
Create and schedule social media posts promoting activities, events and opportunities.
Gather stories, photographs and information from meetings and events to support engaging communications.
About You 
We are looking for someone who is approachable, proactive and highly organised, with the confidence to communicate with a wide range of people and manage a varied workload.
You will ideally have:
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with a friendly and approachable manner.
Previous experience in administration, meeting organisation or activity coordination.
Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities independently.
The ability to take accurate meeting notes and produce clear, concise written summaries.
Good IT skills, including Microsoft Outlook and Word.
Confidence using newsletters, websites and social media to share information.
A flexible and positive approach, with the ability to work independently and as part of a team.
A full driving licence and the ability to travel regularly throughout East Surrey.
The ability to work from the Oxted office when not attending external meetings or events.

jobs.details_text:
Conservation Project Officer
Do you have a qualification in ecology, conservation, environmental management, community engagement or do you have the equivalent practical experience
This is an amazing opportunity to work on a commissioned project to support existing and emerging Beaver Management and Advisory Groups (BMGs/BAGs).
Position: Conservation Project Officer (internally known as BMAG Support Officer)
Location: Home-based, with planned travel across Britain for meetings and workshops, which may include overnight stays
Hours: Part-time , 4 days per week, schedule to be agreed
Contract: Fixed-term contract until 31st March 2028
Salary: £29,043 pro rata
Closing Date: 5:00pm on Sunday 22nd November 2026. We reserve the right to interview candidates and close the ad ahead of the closing date, should a strong candidate be identified.
Interviews: Online interviews will be held on Tuesday 8th December. During the interview you will be asked a series of questions to assess your experience and skills for the role. A number of the questions will be shared in advance of the interview to give you an opportunity to prepare answers.
All shortlisted candidates will be contacted by Wednesday 2nd December at the latest. If you have not heard from us by this date, please accept our thanks for applying and assume that you were not shortlisted on this occasion.
About the Role 
Working on the commissioned project alongside Devon Wildlife Trust, you will support existing and emerging Beaver Management and Advisory Groups (BMGs/BAGs). Funding for the role is provided by Natural England.
Responsibilities include developing governance, stakeholder engagement and risk assessment templates; producing case studies and guidance resources; delivering workshops, training and professional development; and supporting project coordination, evaluation and reporting.
Working collaboratively with groups and partners, you will share best practice, build capabilities and support sustainable working practices, rather than directly delivering beaver management interventions.
Home-based, with planned travel across Britain for meetings and workshops, which may include overnight stays. Travel, accommodation and subsistence expenses will be met in accordance with the Trust’s Expenses Policy. You may occasionally be required to access beaver wetlands or sites but this is not a key part of the role
About You 
We are looking for someone with:
Relevant qualification in ecology, conservation, environmental management, community engagement or equivalent practical experience.
Good understanding of beaver ecology, management and coexistence in Britain, including the role of BMGs/BAGs in coordinating local and catchment-level responses, or demonstrable ability to develop this knowledge quickly.
Good understanding of the policy and regulatory context for beaver management and river restoration in England, including the roles of statutory agencies, local authorities and Catchment Partnerships, or demonstrable ability to develop this knowledge quickly.
Experience of producing clear reports, guidance, templates, case studies or practical resources that help a range of audiences understand and apply technical information.
Strong communication, facilitation and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to work constructively across organisations and differing perspectives.
Ability to interpret evidence, organise information and communicate technical or policy-related material accessibly.
Experience supporting workshops, peer-learning activities, training or professional development resources.
Competence with standard office software, spreadsheets and online collaboration tools.
Commitment to nature restoration, inclusive engagement, safe working practices and Beaver Trust values.
A safe and secure home-working space and stable internet connection.
Willingness and ability to travel for planned in-person meetings and workshops including overnight stays. Most participating groups are located in the south of England.
We want to hear your own voice, your own experiences and your own way of thinking. Use of assistive tools for spellchecking or grammar is fine, but your application should be written by yourself, and in your own words.
You will be asked to upload a CV and Cover Letter when you apply.
About the Organisation 
Join a nature restoration charity, restoring beavers to regenerate our landscapes. Our client’s team is small with a diverse skillset and extensive experience in beaver ecology and restoration, human-wildlife coexistence, and policy. They provide practical solutions to help people to co-exist with beavers and influence legislation in Scotland, Wales and at Westminster that rebuilds ecosystems, improves river health, and strengthens climate resilience in a time of ecological and climate crisis.
Benefits include:
25 days holiday, plus Christmas day through to New Year’s Day paid, plus 6 days of floating holidays.
Flexible approach to hours of work.
Travel, accommodation and subsistence expenses will be met by the trust in
Pension contribution of 3% of your total pay each month
One-off contributions toward the cost of an ergonomic office chair and toward purchases of essential devices (laptop, mouse and smartphone)
Monthly home working allowance, plus an annual contribution toward the maintenance and/or replacement of the essential devices.
We are committed to inclusive recruitment and are happy to make reasonable adjustments at any stage of the process. We actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, especially those underrepresented in the environmental sector, including people of colour, disabled people, those from low-income backgrounds, LGBTQIA+ communities and all other protected characteristics
You may have experience in roles including Conservation Project Officer, Environmental Project Officer, Conservation Engagement Officer, Conservation Partnerships Officer, Environmental Partnerships Officer, C

jobs.details_text:
Digital Marketing Campaign Manager 
London Bridge – 2 days in office, 3 days remote working 
Up to £47,000 
Hyde is looking for a Digital Campaigns Project Manager to join our commercially focused Sales and Marketing team at Hyde New Homes.
You’ll take ownership of digital marketing across PPC, SEO, social media, email, display, video and our sales website, using data, customer insight and emerging AI tools to increase brand awareness, generate sales enquiries and maximise return on marketing investment in a busy, deadline-driven environment.
Key Duties 
Plan, deliver and optimise digital campaigns across PPC, SEO, Google Search and Display, paid and organic social media, email, display and video.
Manage and improve the Hyde New Homes website and product microsites, ensuring content is engaging, accessible and optimised for search performance and user experience.
Develop email campaigns, landing pages and digital content that increase lead engagement and generate sales enquiries.
Use dashboards and analytics tools to monitor performance, measure return on investment and recommend improvements to marketing activity and spend.
Work with sales colleagues, internal stakeholders, external agencies and website suppliers to deliver campaigns on time and within budget.
Why Join Hyde? 
Hyde is part of the Hyde group, one of the UK’s leading housing providers, managing and owning around 130,000 homes nationwide. We’re committed to building safe, sustainable communities where people can thrive. With a strong social purpose, long-term investment plans and a focus on innovation, Hyde is a place where you can grow your career while making a real difference.
This role provides the opportunity to take ownership of a varied digital marketing portfolio and make a measurable contribution to the success of Hyde New Homes. You will combine commercial thinking, creativity and data to improve campaign performance, strengthen our digital presence and support customers as they explore their home ownership options.
As a Digital Campaigns Project Manager, we’re seeking someone who can bring:
Demonstrable experience planning, delivering and optimising digital marketing campaigns across PPC, SEO, social media and display or video channels.
Strong project management and organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple campaigns, budgets, stakeholders and deadlines.
Experience using performance data and analytics to evaluate campaigns, improve return on investment and make informed recommendations.
Confidence managing websites through WordPress or other content management systems, including content updates, user experience and SEO improvements.
Strong knowledge of AI tools and how they can support website development, SEO and digital content creation, with an interest in emerging marketing technology.
Experience using platforms such as Google Analytics, Google Ads, Google Search Console, Facebook Ads Manager, Hotjar, Datorama, Flipsnack, WordPress, HTML, CSS and email marketing systems would be beneficial.
The Benefits of Joining Hyde 
Excellent pension scheme
Generous holiday allowance
Life assurance
Award-winning flexible benefits platform
Support for learning and career development
Hybrid working options available
Diversity, Inclusion & Accessibility 
Equity, diversity and inclusion are central to life at Hyde. We’re committed to creating a truly inclusive workplace where everyone feels respected, valued and able to be themselves. Our aim is to have a workforce that reflects the diversity of the customers and communities we serve, ensuring that different perspectives are represented in decision-making, service delivery and the way we shape our organisation.
By fostering an environment where all voices are heard and valued, we can better understand the needs of our communities and deliver services that are fair, accessible and impactful.
As a Disability Confident Employer, we’re committed to providing reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process and beyond.
We reserve the right to close this advert early if a suitable candidate is identified.

Job Description Networker & Community Engagement Officer 
(Canterbury & Surrounding areas)
Part Time 22.5hrs | £14,500 pa
Job Purpose 
To develop and implement community and marketing initiatives aligned to Home Instead's mission and values to strengthen the brand and grow our market share.
The role is fully community based and requires candidates to work across Canterbury & surrounding areas.
The Role 
Develop relationships in the local community maintaining a pipeline of opportunities by growing and leveraging your network.
Networking face to face, by phone, email, video call with community stakeholders and potential RPNs (minimum of 35 face to face community networking impressions weekly)
Working to agreed targets for Referral Provider touchpoints.
Deliver promotional activities both face to face and virtually to increase awareness of Home Instead's client services and employment opportunities in the local community.
Build relationships with key RPN's, working to agreed targets and have regular touch points to drive Client and Care Professionals enquiries
Plan and successfully execute regular community marketing events including attending fairs, exhibitions, recruitment events and any other events that would promote our services to the public.
Continually deliver a message that reflects our mission, vision and values and delivers our value proposition.
Plan and coordinate a schedule of activity across social media platforms.
Ensure digital content is engaging and kept up to date.
Develop and maintain knowledge of the Home Instead brand and raise awareness of Home Instead National Office marketing campaigns and recruitment initiatives across the network of relationships that have been built in the local community.
Accurately track and record enquiries and use the information to manage and adjust strategy to optimise messaging and education in the community.
Maintain accurate data and information to analyse own performance. Use data and information to continually assess performance against strategic goals.
Manage own time effectively, prioritising critical tasks and adapt to the changing needs of the business and reacting to new needs or challenges in an effective manner.
Ensure compliance with Home Instead's Equality, Diversity and Equal Opportunities Policy, in respect of employment and service delivery.
Carry out any other duties deemed necessary for the successful operation of the business.

Proven track record in successfully building strong relationships both face to face and virtually within a local community to achieve business objectives using a variety of tools and techniques.
Confident to network face to face, by phone, email, video call with community stakeholders and potential RPNs.
Confident to deliver talks on key ageing subjects such as Dementia, Fraud Prevention, Nutrition & Hydration etc.
Good understanding of marketing principles with experience of using a range of marketing and communication approaches including managing digital media platforms/campaigns.

Effective interpersonal skills with excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to deliver effective and engaging presentations or workshops to a broad-based audience.
Strong organisational and prioritisation skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work independently, use initiative and be resilient.
Ability to work flexibly to meet the needs of the business.
Competent in using a CRM database to manage touchpoints with RPNs.

Job details Details 
Title: Communities & Prevention Officer - Men's Mental Health
Reference: SCC/TP/434049/6225
Positions: 1
Salary: £17,183 per annum (pro rata to £42,958 FTE)
Category: Community Safety
Contract type: Permanent
Working hours: 14.4 hours per week
Posted on: 27 October 2026
Closing date: 18 November 2026
Directorate: Adults, Wellbeing & Health Partnerships
Location: Woodhatch Place, 11 Cockshot Hill, Woodhatch, Reigate, RH2 8EF
Description We are committed to the development of our workforce. This position is only available to applicants who already work for Surrey County Council. We thank you for your interest in our roles and would encourage you to review our vacancies which are open to all.
This permanent role has a starting salary of £17,183 per annum (pro rata to £42,958 FTE), working 14.4 hours per week. 
We have a great opportunity to join our Prevention Innovation team as a Prevention Innovation Officer for Men's Mental Health. The Prevention Innovation Team works at the forefront of community development, leading projects that test new approaches in health & wellbeing. This role will have a focus on East Surrey, and is a hybrid role, allowing flexibility to work from home or the office, as well as working directly within communities.
As a team, we support hybrid working with the right balance. We come together in person for two days per week on average (40% of the working week) and support working from home, or in the community, the rest of the time.
Our Offer to You 
26 days' holiday, rising to 28 days after 2 years' service and 31 days after 5 years' service
Option to buy up to 10 days of additional annual leave
A generous local government salary related pension
Up to 5 days of carer's leave and 2 paid volunteering days per year
Paternity, adoption and dependents leave
An Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) to support health and wellbeing
Learning and development hub where you can access a wealth of resources
Wellbeing and lifestyle discounts including gym, travel, and shopping
A chance to make a real difference to the lives of our residents.
About The Role 
You will be responsible for the ongoing development and coordination of place-based services that support men's mental health & wellbeing. This may include working with community organisations to explore opportunities for expanding the provision of place-based services for men's wellbeing, providing oversight of the day-to-day operation of men's mental health place-based services, and developing the governance and infrastructure to support how men's mental health & wellbeing support is provided to residents in community settings. You will also be required to advise and support partners on the topic of men's mental health and attend events, where relevant, to share about the relevant provisions available.
Over the next 18 months you will be working to secure the sustainability of community-based men's mental health provision. This includes supporting local provisions to become safely volunteer-led, developing and implementing the governance and infrastructure that supports the operation of community-based men's mental health provision, and encouraging community-ownership of these provisions. Where appropriate, you will also work to expand the access and availability of men's mental health community support into areas of demonstrable need. The successful candidate will also support evaluation of men's mental health provision and help make the case for doing more of what works.
This role contributes to toward Surrey's ambitions to tackle health inequality, and create empowered and thriving communities. You will do this by improving access to support services, encouraging community ownership of place-based wellbeing provision, and supporting residents to develop their skills and support others.
Your Application 
In order to be considered for shortlisting, your application will clearly evidence the following skills and align with our behaviours:
Project and programme management, including governance and oversight
Community engagement and volunteer management to support place-based initiatives
Partnership working to deliver positive outcomes across organisations and communities
Effective use of digital tools to improve service delivery and accessibility
Strong communication skills, with the ability to present information clearly and succinctly
Adaptable and empathetic approach, with an understanding of health and social care challenges and a willingness to respond to new insights and opportunities
To apply, we request that you submit a CV and you will be asked the following 4 questions:
Tell us about a time when you worked with a community group, volunteers, or residents to develop or improve a local initiative. What was your role, how did you ensure people felt ownership of the work, and what was the outcome?
Describe a situation where you supported someone or a group whose needs, experiences, or circumstances were different from your own. How did you ensure their voice was heard, and what did you learn from the experience?
Tell us about a time when you identified a better way of working, challenged an existing process, or introduced a new approach. What prompted the change and what impact did it have?
Give an example of a time when you had to bring together different organisations, stakeholders or partners to achieve a shared outcome. How did you manage differing priorities and what was achieved?
Before submitting your application, we recommend you read the job description & Our Life at Surrey handbook to get an insight into working at Surrey.
The job advert closes at 23:59 on 18/11/2026 with interviews planned to follow.

jobs.details_text:
As the UK's leading Social Enterprise, we move lives forward every day by building, managing and supporting thriving Communities. From new homes, social housing and student accommodation to leisure, education and Community initiatives, our work makes a positive difference to millions of People across the UK. And that takes People who care about doing the right thing. People who are ambitious, ready to grow and motivated to make a difference through the work they do.
We're looking for colleagues who bring energy, curiosity and ownership. People who enjoy being challenged, support those around them and want to keep raising the bar. Because when we perform at our best, we create more opportunities to invest in our customers, our communities and each other.
Experience matters, but it's only part of the story. If you share our values and want to build a career where your work has real impact, we'd love to hear from you.
More about your role 
As a Community Housing Manager, you'll deliver a customer-focused housing management service across a regional patch, taking ownership of tenancy and neighbourhood issues and finding practical solutions for our customers. You'll regularly inspect communal areas, manage cases of anti-social behaviour and tenancy breaches, support customers to sustain their tenancies and help ensure our communities remain safe and well maintained. You'll also oversee service charge budgets for the schemes you manage, work closely with internal teams and external partners, and identify and support vulnerable customers through our safeguarding procedures.
This role will cover Hampshire and the Isle of Wight.
Essential criteria 
To be considered for this role, you'll need:
Previous experience working within the housing management experience across different rented tenures, with an understanding of tenancy law.
Experience delivering housing, tenancy or neighbourhood management services within a customer-focused organisation.
Experience managing housing-related issues such as anti-social behaviour, tenancy breaches, safeguarding or tenancy sustainment.
A CIH Housing Certificate would be an advantage and/or the desire to work towards the qualification
A valid full driving licence and access to a vehicle
More about you 
You'll have a strong understanding of the issues that can affect customers and their tenancies, including safeguarding and the needs of vulnerable customers. You'll be comfortable taking ownership of cases, using your initiative to solve problems and working with a diverse range of people. Knowledge of tenancy and estate management, experience building effective partnerships with other agencies and confidence using Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams and Outlook will help you succeed in the role.
What you'll get 
We know rewarding work deserves rewarding benefits. That's why, alongside a competitive salary, you'll have access to a package designed to support you at work and beyond. You'll receive:
Pension with matched contributions up to 7%
Bonus scheme for colleagues at 2%
35 days holiday (including bank holidays) pro rata with the option to buy or sell days
Healthcare cashback plan for everyday medical costs, with private GP and health support services available
Comprehensive wellbeing support including counselling, flu jabs, our Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) and access to our Wellbeing Hub, supporting your mental, physical and financial wellbeing
Access to Our Place Rewards, offering discounts and savings on groceries, travel, shopping, home products and other lifestyle purchases
Ongoing training, professional qualifications, internal development programmes and career progression opportunities
Recognition programmes including Star Awards and Colleague Awards, celebrating achievements and recognising great work
Strong focus on inclusion, wellbeing and colleague engagement
Free membership to Places Gyms
Life Assurance to provide financial security for your loved ones, alongside access to will writing services to help you plan for the future with confidence
What's next? 
If you meet the criteria and are ready to make the next step in your career then click apply. You will be redirected to our careers site where you can discover more about the role, read a full job description and apply directly to us.
As part of our commitment to diversity and inclusion, we offer a guaranteed interview to candidates who are disabled, neurodiverse, or have served in the Armed Forces, provided they meet the essential criteria for the role. If you would like to be considered under this scheme, please indicate this in your application. We are dedicated to creating a supportive and accessible recruitment process for all.
We are committed to creating an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. If you require any reasonable adjustments to support your application or interview experience, please let us know. We're happy to work with you to ensure you have the opportunity to perform at your best.
If you are a Places for People customer and you're looking for support with your application, please contact our skills and employment team on .
W e understand the importance of a supportive and inclusive work culture so please talk to us at interview about flexibility you may need. We can't promise to give you exactly what you want, but we promise not to judge you for asking. For this role we are open to discussing the possibility of reduced hours, flexible start and finish times or compressed hours. 
If you are a recruitment agency please note we operate a PSL and do not take cold calls

At Places for People, safeguarding is everyone's responsibility. We are committed to creating safe communities for our customers and colleagues by protecting children, young people, and adults at risk from harm, abuse, and neglect.

jobs.details_text:
Communications Officer (Social Media) 
Location: Hybrid
Salary: FTE £25,000 to £26,500 per annum
Role Status: 28 to 35 hours per week
Closing Date: 19 Nov 2026
Are you creative, curious and passionate about using social media to make a difference
Meningitis Now is looking for a Communications Officer (Social Media) to join our Communications team and help us reach, engage and inspire audiences across our social media channels. Whether you're a recent graduate or have gained experience through college, volunteering or a junior communications role, we'll support you to develop your skills and grow within the charity.
You'll help bring our work to life online by creating engaging content, sharing powerful stories, supporting campaigns and building meaningful connections with our community.
About the Job 
Working closely with colleagues across the charity, you'll help manage our social media channels and create engaging content that raises awareness of meningitis, supports fundraising and showcases the impact of our work. You'll be encouraged to bring fresh ideas, spot new trends and help us reach new audiences through creative digital communications.
Key responsibilities:
Day-to-day management of Meningitis Now's social media channels, including Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and TikTok.
Create and schedule engaging social media content, including posts, stories, reels, videos and graphics.
Manage and moderate online communities, responding to comments and messages in a timely and sensitive way.
Work with colleagues to promote fundraising activities, awareness campaigns, support services and events.
Manage paid social media campaigns, working with third-party suppliers where appropriate.
Monitor social media performance and contribute to reporting and campaign evaluation.
Keep up to date with social media trends and help identify new opportunities for engagement.
Support wider communications, marketing and campaign activities when needed.
What We're Looking For 
Essential:
Excellent written communication skills and attention to detail.
A passion for social media and digital communication.
Creativity and an eye for engaging content.
Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple tasks.
Confidence using major social media platforms.
Ability to work collaboratively with a wide range of people.
An understanding of how social media can help organisations build awareness and engagement.
Desirable:
Experience creating content for social media, whether through work, study, volunteering or personal projects.
Basic knowledge of design tools such as Canva or Adobe Creative Suite.
Experience creating short-form video content and reels.
An interest in the charity sector.
Ready to Apply 
Please apply by completing the application form on our HR system – you will be redirected on clicking apply.
Please note that due to using an anonymised recruitment process, only responses to the application questions will be used for shortlisting. If you choose to upload a CV or covering letter, this information won't be seen until after shortlisting has been completed.
Closing date for applications: 9am, Thursday, 19 November 2026
Interviews: Tuesday, 1 December 2026
*Note: Meningitis Now reserve the right to close this advert early or extend it depending on the number of sufficient applications received. If you are interested, please apply as soon as possible.

This is an opportunity to help shape a role from the beginning.
jobs.details_text:
Location: Hybrid role - flexible across all regions with link to nearest office base
Salary: London - £50,849 - £63,561 per annum / National - £46,885 - £58,607 per annum
Hours: 36 per week 
Contract Type: Permanent
At Clarion, we believe everyone deserves to feel safe, supported and secure in their home. We're introducing a new kind of social work role.
What if housing and social care worked together around the person, rather than residents having to navigate the boundaries between different organisations?
We want to help make that happen. We're creating a new Social Worker (Housing) role, bringing professional social work expertise directly into our housing environment and helping us build stronger connections between housing, adult social care, health, safeguarding and community services.
This is an opportunity to help shape a role from the beginning. You'll work alongside housing colleagues and external partners to find solutions for residents whose circumstances cannot be addressed by housing intervention alone. Your focus will be on understanding the whole person, their home, strengths, relationships, risks and aspirations, and bringing the right organisations together around them.
What you'll do 
You'll bring a professional social work perspective to some of the situations where housing, health and social care intersect.
This role will provide specialist social work expertise to support residents experiencing vulnerability, helping them achieve positive outcomes through strengths-based, person-centred practice. You'll undertake holistic assessments, identify risks and support needs, and work with residents to develop practical solutions where housing and social care issues are closely connected. You'll build strong relationships with statutory and community partners, including Adult Social Care, the NHS, mental health services and safeguarding teams, ensuring coordinated and effective support for residents.
The successful candidate will contribute to complex case discussions, safeguarding processes and multi-agency planning, bringing professional knowledge of the Care Act 2014, Mental Capacity Act 2005 and adult safeguarding principles into a housing setting. You'll also support colleagues to navigate social care pathways, identify opportunities to improve partnership working, and use learning from individual cases to influence service development and improve outcomes across the organisation.
The role will seek to strengthen the interface between housing, social care, health and the voluntary and community sector, enabling partners to build solutions around residents rather than organisational boundaries. That means developing relationships with partners, understanding their statutory responsibilities and pressures, and creating routes through which information, professional expertise and interventions can come together around the resident.
The person we're looking for 
We're looking for someone who is professionally curious, practical and determined to make systems work better for people. You'll be comfortable moving between two worlds: understanding the statutory framework and professional standards of social work while recognising the realities of housing management and tenancy sustainment.
You won't simply identify why something cannot be done. You'll help residents and partners work out what can be done, who needs to be involved and how we get there.
You'll be able to challenge constructively, influence across organisational boundaries and build relationships with professionals from different disciplines while keeping the resident's voice at the centre.
We would be especially interested in experience involving adult social care, mental health, safeguarding adults, older people, learning disabilities, autism and neurodiversity, physical disability, self-neglect and hoarding, homelessness or housing instability, domestic abuse, substance use, hospital discharge, community-based social work and multi-agency risk management.
If you're a qualified social worker who wants to use your professional expertise differently and help redesign the relationship between housing and social care, we'd like to hear from you.

jobs.details_text:
Digital Communications Executive 
Salary: £32,630 per annum
Contract: 12-month fixed-term
Work Pattern: Full Time, 37.5 hours per week, Monday to Friday
Location: WWT Slimbridge GL2. We support hybrid working.
About The Role 
We’re looking for a Digital Communications Executive who combines technical know-how with a genuine understanding of people, and who puts their colleagues and supporters at the heart of every decision.
You'll be the go-to person for colleagues across WWT, helping them get the most from our digital tools and supporting them in making our digital channels work as best they can, to help WWT thrive.
Through your work, you'll play a key role in connecting more people with wetlands, inspiring action for nature and helping WWT restore wetlands and unlock their power for people and wildlife.
About You 
To be successful in this role, you’ll have:
A desire to help others, with the patience, empathy and good humour to support colleagues and get satisfaction from enabling wider teams to do their best work.
Excellent written, verbal and visual communication skills, with the ability to listen carefully, ask the right questions, explain technical concepts clearly and confidently support non-technical colleagues in using digital platforms.
Significant experience in a digital communications, digital marketing or web content role, including planning, building and maintaining content in a content management system.
Hands-on experience building, testing and sending email campaigns, and using analytics to measure performance and keep improving results.
Working knowledge of HTML and CSS and image editing software (such as Photoshop), with a solid grasp of SEO, usability and accessible, inclusive web and email content.
A genuine understanding of supporters, with a track record of putting them first and using insight, feedback and analytics to shape content and journeys that work for real people.
Experience working with external agencies, suppliers or freelancers to deliver digital projects on time and within budget.
Strong organisational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to balance competing priorities from fundraising, marketing and communications teams and pick up live work quickly.
About Us 
We’re WWT, and we’re on a mission to restore the super-powered ecosystems we call wetlands. There’s never been a more important moment for our work, and we’ve got some phenomenal people on the case.
Whether they’re taking a new visitor under their wing, or conducting ground-breaking research further afield, our team are second to none. And there’s nothing we love more than watching them soar.
Whatever you do here, you’ll be helping to restore wetlands and unlock their power. So, the only question left is, what role will you play?
Why you’ll love working at WWT 
Wake up every day knowing your work is helping to restore wetlands, and our world
Be surrounded and inspired by our team of passionate, dedicated people
33 days annual leave (which goes up to 38 days after 5 years of service) – this includes bank holidays and you have flexibility to take those days whenever you want
Free entry to all our wetland centres, including your family
Free car parking and secure bike storage areas
Colleague discount on shopping and memberships
Cycle to work scheme
Contributory pension scheme
Life Assurance of three times your salary, for peace of mind for your loved ones
Independent personal, workplace and financial advice from Care first
Additional Information 
This is a full time, 12-month fixed-term contract working 37.5 hours per week, Monday-Friday. Based at WWT Slimbridge Wetland Centre, with the opportunity for hybrid working. The role will be required to be at Slimbridge at least once a week and as required for key meetings.
Closing Date: Monday 30th November 2026 
N.B. We reserve the right to close the advert early if we receive a sufficient number of applications from candidates who meet the required skills and experience. We therefore encourage early applications.
Interested? 
If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. 
WWT is an equal opportunities employer and all applications will be considered solely on merit.
No agencies please.

jobs.details_text:
Job Title: Internal Communications Executive
Location: London
Salary: £30,000-37,000
Job Type: Permanent, Full Time
Closing Date: 10th November 2026
About SYNLAB: 
Our people support pathology services that matter to patients, clinicians and communities. Your work will help the Internal Communications team connect colleagues across our headquarters and four hospital businesses.
As part of our Marketing & Communications team, you will work alongside specialists in internal, corporate, service-user and social communications. You will support colleagues on a broad mix of activity and gain exposure to senior stakeholders and functions including Operations, IT, Quality, Health and Safety, Finance, People, Learning and Development, Recruitment and scientific development.
You will join us at an important stage in the development of our communications channels, including the launch of a UK&I-wide intranet. You will help deliver these improvements by coordinating activity, creating content, gathering feedback and contributing ideas. You will have the support and direction of experienced colleagues while being trusted to take responsibility for your work and follow tasks through to completion.
About the Role: 
Can you turn complex business updates into communications that people genuinely want to read, watch and act on? 
We are looking for an experienced Internal Communications Executive to provide creative and practical support to our Internal Communications team. You will help us keep more than 3,000 colleagues across SYNLAB UK&I informed, connected and clear about our strategy, priorities and the part they play in our success.
Working within agreed plans and priorities, you will turn ideas into action by creating audience-focused content, coordinating activity and supporting campaigns across our channels. You will be trusted to manage your own workload, take initiative and keep projects moving, while working closely with the Internal Communications Manager and wider Communications team.
Based at our Blackfriars Hub three days a week, with travel to other SYNLAB businesses across the UK, you will join a collaborative team of nine. If you have relevant experience and want to broaden your skills through varied, hands-on work, this role will give you the opportunity to contribute ideas, support high-profile projects and make a visible difference to how colleagues experience communications.
Working under the direction of the Internal Communications Manager, you will support the planning, coordination and delivery of communications across the organisation.
You will manage the communications calendar, coordinate requests, track actions and approvals, and help ensure timely, well-sequenced communications. Working across multiple priorities, you will create and publish content for the intranet, newsletters, digital signage, town halls, presentations and video, while supporting key employee campaigns and initiatives.
You will also help engage colleagues in laboratory and other non-desk-based roles, gathering feedback and ensuring communications reach all audiences effectively.
What You Will Do: 
Deliver timely, accurate and engaging internal communications, effectively managing competing priorities, stakeholder requests and deadlines while supporting the Internal Communications Manager and wider Communications team to achieve business objectives.
Maintain and continuously develop internal communication channels, including the intranet, newsletters, digital signage, town halls and other employee communication platforms, ensuring content is consistent, relevant and engaging.
Own and manage the internal communications calendar, coordinating content, campaigns and key messaging across the business.
Create, write, coordinate and deliver internal communications campaigns that support organisational priorities, projects and initiatives, including DE&I, ESG, appraisal cycles and employee recognition programmes.
Build strong relationships and networks across the organisation to proactively identify, develop and share engaging employee, business and customer stories.
Collaborate with internal and external communications colleagues to maximise content and engagement opportunities arising from events, conferences, awards, town halls, site visits and other key activities.
